-- Example: a stepper. Up and down change the value. Left and right change the step. OK clears the value.
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.calc then
    ctx.state.calc = { value = 0, step = 1 }
  end
  return ctx.state.calc
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.key == "up" then s.value = s.value + s.step
  elseif ev.key == "down" then s.value = s.value - s.step
  elseif ev.key == "left" then s.step = math.max(1, math.floor(s.step / 10))
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.step = math.min(1000, s.step * 10)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then s.value = 0
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(24, math.floor(w * 0.06))
  local result_h = math.floor(h * 0.42)
  g:clear(0)
  g:rect(margin, margin, w - margin * 2, result_h, "fill", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + 28, "VALUE", { color = 0 })
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + math.floor(result_h * 0.45), tostring(s.value), { color = 0 })
  g:rect(margin, margin + result_h + 16, w - margin * 2, 72, "stroke", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + result_h + 40, "STEP " .. tostring(s.step), { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: read lines from a file declared in manifest.data_files. Progress stays in ctx.state.
local FILE = "items.tsv"

local function tr(ctx, key)
  if ctx.i18n and ctx.i18n.t then return ctx.i18n:t(key) end
  return key
end

function on_load(ctx)
  ctx.items = {}
  local reader = ctx.data:open_text(FILE)
  if not reader then return end
  reader:read_line()
  while true do
    local line = reader:read_line()
    if not line then break end
    local label, value = line:match("([^\t]+)\t([^\t]+)")
    if label then ctx.items[#ctx.items + 1] = { label = label, value = value } end
  end
  reader:close()
  if not ctx.state.index then ctx.state.index = 1 end
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" or #ctx.items == 0 then return false end
  if ev.key == "down" or ev.key == "ok" then ctx.state.index = ctx.state.index % #ctx.items + 1
  elseif ev.key == "up" then ctx.state.index = (ctx.state.index - 2) % #ctx.items + 1
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 24, tr(ctx, "title"), { color = 15 })
  local item = ctx.items[ctx.state.index or 1]
  if item then
    g:text(24, 90, item.label, { color = 15 })
    g:text(24, 130, item.value, { color = 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: the swap writes the final board immediately. on_tick only advances original, blank, and settled.
local PHASE_MS = { original = 400, blank = 500, settled = 400 }

local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.grid then
    ctx.state.grid = {
      board = { 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 },
      cursor = 3,
      animation = nil,
    }
  end
  return ctx.state.grid
end

local function clone(board)
  local copy = {}
  for index = 1, 9 do copy[index] = board[index] end
  return copy
end

local function full_row(board)
  for row = 0, 2 do
    local a = row * 3 + 1
    if board[a] == 1 and board[a + 1] == 1 and board[a + 2] == 1 then
      return { a, a + 1, a + 2 }
    end
  end
  return nil
end

local function adjacent(a, b)
  local ar, ac = math.floor((a - 1) / 3), (a - 1) % 3
  local br, bc = math.floor((b - 1) / 3), (b - 1) % 3
  return math.abs(ar - br) + math.abs(ac - bc) == 1
end

local function resolve_swap(board, a, b)
  if not adjacent(a, b) then return nil end
  local before = clone(board)
  before[a], before[b] = before[b], before[a]
  local cells = full_row(before)
  if not cells then return nil end
  local after = clone(before)
  for _, cell in ipairs(cells) do after[cell] = 0 end
  return { before = before, cells = cells, after = after, phase = "original", remaining = PHASE_MS.original }
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local animation = s.animation
  if not animation then return end
  animation.remaining = animation.remaining - (dt_ms or 0)
  if animation.remaining > 0 then return end
  if animation.phase == "original" then
    animation.phase = "blank"
    animation.remaining = PHASE_MS.blank
  elseif animation.phase == "blank" then
    animation.phase = "settled"
    animation.remaining = PHASE_MS.settled
    s.board = animation.after
  else
    s.animation = nil
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.animation then return false end
  if ev.key == "left" then s.cursor = s.cursor - ((s.cursor - 1) % 3 == 0 and 0 or 1)
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.cursor = s.cursor + ((s.cursor - 1) % 3 == 2 and 0 or 1)
  elseif ev.key == "up" then s.cursor = math.max(1, s.cursor - 3)
  elseif ev.key == "down" then s.cursor = math.min(9, s.cursor + 3)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then
    local partner = s.cursor < 9 and s.cursor + 1 or s.cursor - 1
    s.animation = resolve_swap(s.board, s.cursor, partner)
    if not s.animation then return false end
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local board = s.board
  local hidden = {}
  if s.animation and s.animation.phase == "blank" then
    board = s.animation.before
    for _, cell in ipairs(s.animation.cells) do hidden[cell] = true end
  elseif s.animation and s.animation.phase == "original" then
    board = s.animation.before
  end
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 24, "SWAP WITH RIGHT", { color = 15 })
  local origin_x, origin_y, cell = 24, 70, 72
  for index = 1, 9 do
    local column = (index - 1) % 3
    local row = math.floor((index - 1) / 3)
    local x = origin_x + column * (cell + 8)
    local y = origin_y + row * (cell + 8)
    local selected = index == s.cursor
    g:rect(x, y, cell, cell, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    if not hidden[index] and board[index] == 1 then
      g:circle(x + 36, y + 36, 16, "fill", selected and 0 or 15)
    end
  end
end

-- Example: one rectangle function for drawing and hit testing. The focused card is inverted.
local LABELS = { "NOW", "NEXT", "LATER", "NOTES" }

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.cards = ctx.state.cards or { selected = 1, opened = 0 }
  return ctx.state.cards
end

local function layout(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(20, math.floor(w * 0.05))
  local gap = 12
  local card_w = math.floor((w - margin * 2 - gap) / 2)
  local card_h = math.floor((h - margin * 2 - gap) * 0.42)
  return { margin = margin, gap = gap, card_w = card_w, card_h = card_h, cards_y = margin + 36 }
end

local function card_position(l, index)
  local column = (index - 1) % 2
  local row = math.floor((index - 1) / 2)
  local x = l.margin + column * (l.card_w + l.gap)
  local y = l.cards_y + row * (l.card_h + l.gap)
  return x, y
end

local function hit_card(l, x, y)
  for index = 1, 4 do
    local left, top = card_position(l, index)
    if x >= left and x <= left + l.card_w and y >= top and y <= top + l.card_h then
      return index
    end
  end
  return nil
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "left" then s.selected = s.selected - ((s.selected - 1) % 2 == 0 and 0 or 1)
    elseif ev.key == "right" then s.selected = s.selected + ((s.selected - 1) % 2 == 1 and 0 or 1)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then s.selected = math.max(1, s.selected - 2)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.selected = math.min(4, s.selected + 2)
    elseif ev.key == "ok" then s.opened = s.selected
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    local index = hit_card(layout(ctx), ev.x or 0, ev.y or 0)
    if not index then return false end
    s.selected = index
    s.opened = index
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local l = layout(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(l.margin, 24, s.opened > 0 and ("OPEN " .. LABELS[s.opened]) or "PICK A CARD", { color = 15 })
  for index = 1, 4 do
    local x, y = card_position(l, index)
    local selected = index == s.selected
    g:rect(x, y, l.card_w, l.card_h, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 16, y + 28, LABELS[index], { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: seven-segment digits from g:rect, with a static panel on an offscreen layer.
local panel

local DIGIT_SEGMENTS = {
  ["0"] = "abcdef", ["1"] = "bc", ["2"] = "abdeg", ["3"] = "abcdg",
  ["4"] = "bcfg", ["5"] = "acdfg", ["6"] = "acdefg", ["7"] = "abc",
  ["8"] = "abcdefg", ["9"] = "abcdfg",
}

local function has_segment(segments, name)
  return segments and string.find(segments, name, 1, true) ~= nil
end

local function draw_digit(g, x, y, digit, scale, color)
  local segments = DIGIT_SEGMENTS[digit]
  local t, w, h = 8 * scale, 46 * scale, 80 * scale
  local half = math.floor(h / 2)
  local vertical_h = half - t
  if has_segment(segments, "a") then g:rect(x + t, y, w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "b") then g:rect(x + w - t, y + t, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "c") then g:rect(x + w - t, y + half, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "d") then g:rect(x + t, y + h - t, w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "e") then g:rect(x, y + half, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "f") then g:rect(x, y + t, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "g") then g:rect(x + t, y + half - math.floor(t / 2), w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
end

local function draw_colon(g, x, y, scale, color)
  local dot = 8 * scale
  g:rect(x, y + 20 * scale, dot, dot, "fill", color)
  g:rect(x, y + 52 * scale, dot, dot, "fill", color)
end

local function two_digits(value)
  if value < 10 then return "0" .. tostring(value) end
  return tostring(value)
end

function on_load(ctx)
  panel = ctx.layers:create(320, 160)
  panel:draw_with(function(g)
    g:rect(0, 0, 320, 160, "stroke", 15)
    g:line(20, 124, 300, 124, 15)
  end)
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
  local key = clock.valid and string.format("%02d%02d", clock.hour, clock.minute) or "unset"
  if key ~= ctx.state.shown_minute then
    ctx.state.shown_minute = key
    ctx:invalidate()
  end
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
  local time = clock.valid and (two_digits(clock.hour) .. two_digits(clock.minute)) or "----"
  local scale, digit_w, gap, colon_w = 1, 46, 8, 18
  local time_w = digit_w * 4 + gap * 3 + colon_w
  local x = math.floor((ctx.screen.width - time_w) / 2)
  local y = math.floor((ctx.screen.height - 160) / 2)

  g:clear(0)
  g:layer(panel, math.floor((ctx.screen.width - 320) / 2), y - 40)
  draw_digit(g, x, y, string.sub(time, 1, 1), scale, 15)
  draw_digit(g, x + digit_w + gap, y, string.sub(time, 2, 2), scale, 15)
  draw_colon(g, x + digit_w * 2 + gap * 2, y, scale, 15)
  local right_x = x + digit_w * 2 + gap * 2 + colon_w
  draw_digit(g, right_x, y, string.sub(time, 3, 3), scale, 15)
  draw_digit(g, right_x + digit_w + gap, y, string.sub(time, 4, 4), scale, 15)
end

function on_unload(ctx)
  if panel then panel:dispose() end
end

-- Example: buttons are rebuilt from the current rule. The public view omits other seats' cards.
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.hand then
    ctx.state.hand = {
      mine = { 3, 9, 12 },
      remain = { 3, 5, 4 },
      target = 8,
      selected = 1,
    }
  end
  return ctx.state.hand
end

local function public_view(s)
  return { own = s.mine, remain = s.remain, target = s.target }
end

local function actions(s)
  local view = public_view(s)
  local card = view.own[s.selected]
  if not card or card <= view.target then
    return { { id = "pass", label = "PASS" } }
  end
  return {
    { id = "play", label = "PLAY" },
    { id = "pass", label = "PASS" },
  }
end

local function apply(s, id)
  local row = actions(s)
  local allowed = false
  for _, action in ipairs(row) do
    if action.id == id then allowed = true end
  end
  if not allowed then return end
  if id == "play" then
    table.remove(s.mine, s.selected)
    s.selected = math.max(1, math.min(s.selected, #s.mine))
    s.remain[1] = #s.mine
    s.target = 0
  end
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  local row = actions(s)
  if ev.key == "left" then s.selected = math.max(1, s.selected - 1)
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.selected = math.min(#s.mine, s.selected + 1)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then apply(s, row[1] and row[1].id or "pass")
  elseif ev.key == "back" and row[2] then apply(s, row[2].id)
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local view = public_view(s)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 28, "TARGET " .. tostring(view.target), { color = 15 })
  g:text(24, 64, "OTHERS " .. table.concat(view.remain, " "), { color = 15 })
  local x = 24
  for index, card in ipairs(view.own) do
    local selected = index == s.selected
    g:rect(x, 110, 64, 88, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 18, 146, tostring(card), { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
    x = x + 76
  end
  local row = actions(s)
  local button_w = math.floor((w - 24 * 2 - 12 * (#row - 1)) / math.max(1, #row))
  for index, action in ipairs(row) do
    local left = 24 + (index - 1) * (button_w + 12)
    g:rect(left, 230, button_w, 56, index == 1 and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(left + 16, 250, action.label, { color = index == 1 and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: ctx.longtask:start, then ctx.longtask:feed on a wall-clock budget. Return without stop().
local BUDGET_MS = 2000
local FEED_EVERY_MS = 1000

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.search = ctx.state.search or { best = 0, done = false }
  return ctx.state.search
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.done then return end
  local started_ok, start_err = ctx.longtask:start()
  if started_ok ~= true then
    s.best = 0
    s.done = true
    s.err = tostring(start_err or "inactive")
    ctx:invalidate()
    return
  end
  local started = ctx.sys:millis() or 0
  local fed_at = started
  local best = 0
  for step = 1, 40 do
    local now = ctx.sys:millis() or started
    if now - started >= BUDGET_MS then break end
    best = step
    if now - fed_at >= FEED_EVERY_MS then
      local fed_ok, feed_err = ctx.longtask:feed()
      if fed_ok ~= true then
        error("watchdog feed failed: " .. tostring(feed_err or "inactive"), 0)
      end
      fed_at = now
    end
  end
  s.best = best
  s.done = true
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 48, s.done and ("BEST " .. tostring(s.best)) or "SEARCH", { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: start one GET, poll it from on_tick, and cancel it on leave.
-- The manifest must declare net.http. example.test is only a shape, not a live service.
local URL = "http://example.test/status"
local task_id

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.net = ctx.state.net or { status = "idle", body = "" }
  return ctx.state.net
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.status == "idle" and not task_id then
    local id, err = ctx.net:get(URL)
    if id then
      task_id = id
      s.status = "loading"
    else
      s.status = "error"
      s.body = tostring(err or "request failed")
    end
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  if not task_id then return end
  local result = ctx.net:poll(task_id)
  if not result or not result.done then return end
  local s = state(ctx)
  task_id = nil
  if result.ok then
    s.status = "ready"
    s.body = tostring(result.body or "")
  else
    s.status = "error"
    s.body = tostring(result.err or result.status or "failed")
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  if task_id then ctx.net:cancel(task_id) end
  task_id = nil
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 40, s.status, { color = 15 })
  if s.body ~= "" then g:text(24, 88, s.body, { color = 15 }) end
end

-- Example: list, read, and reveal are three values of screen.
local LINES = {
  "The river is wide.",
  "A lamp marks the pier.",
  "You can still turn back.",
}

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.pages = ctx.state.pages or { screen = "list", recite = 0 }
  return ctx.state.pages
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.screen == "list" then
    if ev.key == "ok" then s.screen = "read"; s.recite = 0
    else return false end
  elseif s.screen == "read" then
    if ev.key == "ok" or ev.key == "down" then s.screen = "recite"; s.recite = 0
    elseif ev.key == "back" then s.screen = "list"
    else return false end
  else
    if ev.key == "ok" or ev.key == "down" then
      s.recite = math.min(#LINES, s.recite + 1)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then
      s.recite = math.max(0, s.recite - 1)
    elseif ev.key == "back" then
      s.screen = "read"
    else return false end
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear(0)
  if s.screen == "list" then
    g:text(24, 48, "ONE POEM", { color = 15 })
    g:text(24, 96, "OK TO OPEN", { color = 15 })
    return
  end
  g:text(24, 36, s.screen == "recite" and "REVEAL" or "READ", { color = 15 })
  for index, line in ipairs(LINES) do
    local y = 80 + (index - 1) * 48
    if s.screen == "recite" and index > s.recite then
      g:line(24, y + 16, math.min(w - 24, 24 + #line * 12), y + 16, 15)
    else
      g:text(24, y, line, { color = 15 })
    end
  end
end

-- Example: a counter stored in ctx.state. Up and down change it. OK resets it.
local function app_state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.counter then ctx.state.counter = 0 end
  return ctx.state
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local state = app_state(ctx)
  if ev.key == "up" then state.counter = state.counter + 1 end
  if ev.key == "down" then state.counter = math.max(0, state.counter - 1) end
  if ev.key == "ok" then state.counter = 0 end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local state = app_state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(24, math.floor(w * 0.06))
  g:clear(0)
  g:rect(margin, margin, w - margin * 2, math.floor(h * 0.55), "stroke", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + 28, "VALUE", { color = 15 })
  g:text(margin + 20, math.floor(h * 0.38), tostring(state.counter), { color = 15 })
  g:text(margin + 20, h - margin - 28, "UP +  DOWN -  OK RESET", { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: nodes and choices live in one table. Drawing and hit testing share choice rectangles.
local STORY = {
  start = {
    text = "A light is on at the end of the pier.",
    choices = {
      { label = "Walk closer", next = "pier" },
      { label = "Stay here", next = "stay" },
    },
  },
  pier = { text = "The lamp is warm. The path ends here.", choices = {} },
  stay = { text = "You wait. The light does not move.", choices = {} },
}

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.story = ctx.state.story or { node = "start", focus = 1 }
  return ctx.state.story
end

local function choice_rect(ctx, index, count)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = 24
  local slot_h = 64
  local y = h - margin - (count - index + 1) * slot_h
  return margin, y, w - margin * 2, slot_h - 8
end

local function hit_choice(ctx, count, x, y)
  for index = 1, count do
    local left, top, width, height = choice_rect(ctx, index, count)
    if x >= left and x <= left + width and y >= top and y <= top + height then
      return index
    end
  end
  return nil
end

local function choose(s, index)
  local node = STORY[s.node]
  local choice = node and node.choices and node.choices[index]
  if not choice then return false end
  s.node = choice.next
  s.focus = 1
  return true
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local choices = (STORY[s.node] and STORY[s.node].choices) or {}
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "up" then s.focus = math.max(1, s.focus - 1)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.focus = math.min(math.max(1, #choices), s.focus + 1)
    elseif ev.key == "ok" then
      if not choose(s, s.focus) then return false end
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    local index = hit_choice(ctx, #choices, ev.x or 0, ev.y or 0)
    if not index or not choose(s, index) then return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local node = STORY[s.node]
  local choices = node.choices or {}
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 48, node.text, { color = 15 })
  for index, choice in ipairs(choices) do
    local x, y, width, height = choice_rect(ctx, index, #choices)
    local selected = index == s.focus
    g:rect(x, y, width, height, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 16, y + 22, choice.label, { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: one input starts a countdown across three poses. Session count and total stay in separate fields.
local RAISE_MS = 180
local HIT_MS = 220
local REST_MS = 200
local STRIKE_MS = RAISE_MS + HIT_MS + REST_MS

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.tap = ctx.state.tap or { session = 0, total = 0, goal = 8, strike_ms = 0 }
  return ctx.state.tap
end

local function pose(s)
  if s.strike_ms > HIT_MS + REST_MS then return "raise" end
  if s.strike_ms > REST_MS then return "hit" end
  return "rest"
end

local function strike(s)
  s.total = s.total + 1
  s.session = s.session + 1
  s.strike_ms = STRIKE_MS
  if s.session >= s.goal then
    s.session = 0
  end
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("high")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.strike_ms <= 0 then return end
  s.strike_ms = math.max(0, s.strike_ms - (dt_ms or 0))
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "ok" then strike(s)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then s.goal = math.min(36, s.goal + 4)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.goal = math.max(4, s.goal - 4)
    elseif ev.key == "back" then s.session = 0
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    strike(s)
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local cx, cy = math.floor(w / 2), math.floor(h * 0.46)
  local which = pose(s)
  local bob = which == "raise" and -36 or (which == "hit" and 18 or 0)
  g:clear(0)
  g:circle(cx, cy, 70, "stroke", 15)
  g:rect(cx - 10, cy - 110 + bob, 20, 70, "fill", 15)
  g:circle(cx, cy - 120 + bob, 16, "fill", 15)
  g:text(24, 28, "ROUND " .. tostring(s.session) .. "/" .. tostring(s.goal), { color = 15 })
  g:text(24, h - 48, "TOTAL " .. tostring(s.total), { color = 15 })
end

# 0. General rules, an example, and Manifest

This directory is the author contract for API 2.x. The current minor version is 2.1. `manifest.json` sets `"api": "2.0"` or `"api": "2.1"`. Anything marked 2.1 exists only on a host that implements 2.1; see section 19. The text is split into sections `00`–`27` and appendices A–C. “This document” means the whole set.

1. Every call you write has a determined result. An optional capability is either present as a function or is nil (section 17).
2. One name does one thing. One operation has one spelling.
3. A parameter of the wrong type (a number where a table is required, nil where a string is required) raises a Lua error. The right type with a value outside the stated range returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Device, file, quota, and network failures return `nil, err`.
4. Predicates (`exists`, `is_*`) return only a boolean. A successful command returns nothing. A successful write or release returns true. A query returns the value it looked up.
5. Everything except the optional capabilities listed in section 17 is required of the host.
6. Every rule has a conformance test (section 20). A host is judged by those tests.

Error codes are a closed set. See section 18.

## Numeric parameters

A parameter described as an integer accepts an integer directly. A float that is exactly an integer (for example `240.0` from `w / 2`) is accepted as that integer. Any other float, NaN, or infinity returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

Coordinates and sizes are in `-32768..32767`, unless a narrower range is stated there. Drawing past the canvas is clipped. That is not an error.

A color is an integer `0..15`, an amount of ink: `0` is paper (white), `15` is the darkest ink (black).

An options table may be omitted. Omitting it is the same as an empty table. Fields the call does not recognize are ignored.

## A complete example

```lua
local F, count

function on_load(ctx)
  F = ctx.fonts
  local saved = ctx.storage:read("state.json")
  count = saved and ctx.json:decode(saved).count or 0
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear()
  g:text(w // 2, 40, ctx.i18n:t("title"), { font = F.large, align = "center" })
  g:rect(40, 120, w - 80, 80, { radius = 12 })
  g:text(w // 2, 160, tostring(count), { align = "center", valign = "middle" })
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "pointer" and ev.gesture == "tap"
     or ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "down" and ev.phase == "down" then
    count = count + 1
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false            -- including back: hand control back and leave the app
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  ctx.storage:write("state.json", ctx.json:encode({ count = count }))
end
```

## Manifest

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `api` | `"2.<minor>"`. A minor newer than the host supports is refused at install. See section 19 |
| `app_id` | Application id. 1–63 bytes, character set `[a-z0-9._-]`. Required |
| `display_name` | Display name. A non-empty string. Required |
| `version` | The application's own version string. Required |
| `author` `description` | Strings. May be omitted |
| `app_icon_s` `app_icon_l` `splash` | Packaged image keys. May be omitted. Suggested sizes are in appendix A |
| `entry` | Main script. Defaults to `index.lua` |
| `display.orientation` | `system`, `portrait`, or `landscape`. Defaults to `system` |
| `requires` | Array of strings, listed below. If the device fails any item, the app does not open (open reports `not_supported`; a host that can tell at install time refuses the install) |
| `permissions` | Array of strings: `net` (section 14), `reader` (2.1, section 22). An unknown name is refused at install |
| `preload_assets` | Array of image keys. A key not in the package is refused at install. Decoded before `on_load`; one failure does not block startup, and `ctx.package:image` tries again |
| `data_files` | Data files `ctx.package` may read. An array of `{ name, format, max_bytes }`: `format` is `txt`, `tsv`, or `json`, the extension of `name` matches it, the file lives under the package `data/`, and it does not exceed `max_bytes`. Otherwise both packaging and install fail |
| `ttf_reserve_kb` | Integer 512–4096. Memory for TTF is reserved at the start of the session: either this field is set, or `requires` contains `ttf` (then the default is 2048). Otherwise this session has no TTF (section 7) |
| `lockscreen.entry` | Lock-screen script. Required when a `lockscreen` object is present. A script missing from the package is refused at install |
| `lockscreen.interval_sec` | Integer. Defaults to 60. Clamped to 30–3600 at install |

Names `requires` may use:

| Name | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `pointer` | The device has a touchscreen |
| `up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` | The device has this key built in (a Bluetooth peripheral does not count) |
| `pattern` `image_transform` `ttf` `ui` | Optional capabilities in section 17 |
| `reader` `dialog` `frontlight` `image_decode` | 2.1 optional capabilities in section 17 |
| `lockscreen_timer` | The device can wake on a timer to refresh the lock screen |

An unknown name is refused at install. Every device has `back`; do not list it. The core flow uses only the input `requires` guarantees, plus `back`.

# 1. Language and the sandbox

Lua 5.5, with 32-bit numbers: integers are signed 32-bit integers, and floats are single precision (`float`). The device processor has only single-precision float hardware. 64-bit integers and double precision would be emulated in software, and that is much slower.

- `math.maxinteger` is `2147483647`. `math.mininteger` is `-2147483648`. Integer add, subtract, and multiply wrap in two's complement when they leave the range.
- Integer operations (`+ - * // %`, and bitwise operations) produce integers. `/` and `^` produce floats.
- Single precision has about 7 significant digits. The contiguous integers that are exact stop at `16777216`. Use integers and `//` for coordinates, counts, and amounts of money.

Open standard libraries: `base`, `table`, `string`, `math`, `utf8`, `coroutine`. `math.random` is seeded differently at the start of each session.

Not present as globals: `io`, `os`, `package`, `debug`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, `load`, `print`, `collectgarbage`. `getmetatable("")` returns false. String methods still work.

`require(name)` loads only a script from this package: replace `.` with `/` and append `.lua`. A module runs once per session, then the cached result is returned. A missing module, a name that contains `..`, or a name that starts with `/` raises the Lua error `module 'name' not found`.

## Memory

The script heap is at least 2 MB (not counting `ttf_reserve_kb`). The actual size depends on memory the device still has free. A failed allocation is a Lua error (`not enough memory`) and can be caught with `pcall`. Collection is `ctx.gc` in section 12.

## Errors

An error raised in a callback and not caught, or a callback that runs out of time, ends this session: no further callback runs (including `on_leave`). The host shows an error screen, then returns to the system. Files written before that are kept.

# 2. Lifecycle

A session starts at load and ends at leave. When the session ends the virtual machine is destroyed. The next open is a new session. State continues only through the files in section 9.

Load order: `on_load`, then the host draws the first frame (it calls `on_draw`).

A function that does not exist is skipped.

| Function | When | Limit |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `on_load(ctx)` | The session is loaded | 2000 ms |
| `on_draw(ctx, g)` | A frame needs to be drawn. `g` is this frame's canvas (section 6) | 1500 ms |
| `on_input(ctx, ev)` | A key or a pointer (section 4). Return `true` to say it was handled | 1000 ms |
| `on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)` | Wakes on the `set_tick` period | 1000 ms |
| `on_pause(ctx)` | A system screen covers the app | 1000 ms |
| `on_resume(ctx)` | The cover goes away. The host then redraws one frame | 1000 ms |
| `on_leave(ctx)` | The last callback before the session ends | 1000 ms |

The timer function of `ctx:after`, the completion function of `ctx.net:request` and of `ctx.input:text`, and (2.1) the completion function of `ctx.dialog` are callbacks too. Their limit is 1000 ms.

While paused (from `on_pause` until `on_resume`) the host does not call `on_input`, `on_tick`, timer functions, or completion functions. After `on_resume` returns, the host first redraws one frame, then calls the timer functions and completion functions that came due during the pause, in order.

Any callback may call the interfaces in this document (the canvas is valid only in `on_draw` and `layer:draw`), including starting a network request or setting a timer from `on_load`.

## Time budget

The limit is wall-clock time, measured from the start of the callback. The host checks between Lua instructions. A slow host function (decoding an image, opening a font, reading or writing a file) is not interrupted. The check happens at the next instruction after it returns. Running over the limit aborts that callback. The error text contains `time budget`. After `pcall` catches it, the host raises it again at the next instruction.

```lua
ctx.budget:extend()
```

Moves the deadline of the current callback to 11000 ms after the moment of the call, and returns true, but the deadline is no later than 30000 ms after the callback started. Called from `on_leave`, or outside a callback, it returns `nil, "inactive"`.

Lua on the device is much slower than on a computer. The following are reference values measured on the Gancao X4 Pro / X4 Classic (2026-10-16 firmware), not guarantees: one virtual machine instruction takes about 0.45 µs and newly allocated memory about 0.2 µs per byte, roughly a hundredth of the speed of a desktop browser; library calls such as `string.format` and string concatenation are just as slow. For JSON and private files see sections 10 and 9. A loop that takes a few milliseconds on a computer may take several hundred on the device. When the work in one callback gets close to its limit, split it over several timer callbacks.

## Tick and timers

```lua
ctx:set_tick(ms)
local timer = ctx:after(ms, function(ctx) end)
timer:cancel()
```

`set_tick` sets the period of `on_tick`. `ms` is an integer from 33 to 60000, or 0 to stop. At the start of the session it is 0, and `on_tick` is not called. The period is the target gap between the starts of two `on_tick` calls. If the previous callback has not finished, the next one waits. Missed ticks are not made up. `dt_ms` is the milliseconds since the previous `on_tick` (since `set_tick`, the first time).

Presenting one frame on an e-ink panel takes a few hundred milliseconds. Frames requested while a present is in progress are composed into one frame. The host may call `on_draw` for that frame while the previous one is still refreshing; it draws the state at that moment, and the frame is shown once the previous refresh finishes. The frame rate on the panel is therefore set by presenting: a partial refresh on the Gancao X4 Pro and X4 Classic takes about 650 ms per frame (about 75 ms to render, about 570 ms to refresh), under 1.5 frames per second, so the displacement between two adjacent frames is speed × 0.65 seconds. The frame on which the system inserts its automatic full refresh takes about 1.5 seconds (section 5). Whether `on_tick` keeps running during a present depends on the device: on the X4 Pro it is called on its period as usual; on the X4 Classic, once the next frame is taken, no callback runs until that frame is shown, so while frames are requested back to back there is one `on_tick` per frame and `dt_ms` is about 650. Gancao firmware before 2026-10-16 behaves the same way. Animate by time: advance continuous motion by speed × `dt_ms`. Do not move one fixed step per `on_tick` or `on_draw`, and do not cap `dt_ms` or a single displacement; otherwise the speed differs several times between devices. When the jump between two frames is too large to read as continuous, use a discrete motion by cell or by step, or draw only the start and the end.

The `set_tick` period is rounded to the device's system tick: Gancao firmware ticks every 10 ms, so `set_tick(33)` runs about every 40 ms.

`after` calls the function once after `ms` milliseconds. `ms` is an integer from 1 to 2147483647. At most 32 timers may be pending at once. The 33rd returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. It returns the timer object. `cancel` stops a pending timer from firing and returns nothing. It has no effect on a timer that has already fired or already been cancelled.

Waking only when needed saves power: align a clock face to the next minute with `ctx:after`, and use `set_tick` only for animation.

## How a session ends

Each of the following calls `on_leave` (unless the session has already ended because of an error), then destroys the virtual machine:

| Cause | When |
| --- | --- |
| The app leaves | The script calls `ctx:quit()`, after the current callback returns |
| A system page opens | The script calls `ctx.system:open` (2.1, section 25), after the current callback returns |
| Back was not handled | `on_input` for `back` did not return `true` (section 4) |
| Forced exit | A long press of Back (section 4) |
| The lock screen starts | The system decides to lock (section 15) |
| Power off | The user powers off, or low battery powers off |

When `on_leave` starts, unfinished network exchanges, text input, dialogs, and pending timers are cancelled. Their functions are not called. A file written in `on_leave` is flushed before the virtual machine is destroyed. Within 1000 ms at least 256 KB of writes can finish.

`ctx:quit()` returns nothing.

When a system screen covers the app and a finger is still down, the host delivers a pointer `cancel` first, then `on_pause`.

# 3. Screen and device

```lua
ctx.screen.width
ctx.screen.height
ctx.screen.orientation    -- "portrait" | "landscape"
ctx.screen.occlusion      -- { top, right, bottom, left }, pixels hidden by the bezel
ctx.screen.gray_levels    -- gray levels the app's drawing actually shows
ctx.device.model          -- device profile name, see the table below
ctx.device.lock_timer     -- whether a timer can wake the lock screen (the "timer wake" column), boolean
ctx.device.name           -- 2.1: the name the user gave the device
ctx.device.firmware       -- 2.1: firmware version string
ctx.device.id_for_app     -- 2.1: a device id that differs per app
```

`id_for_app` is 32 lowercase hex characters. On one device the same `app_id` always gets the same value. A different app gets a different value, and a different device gets a different value. Use it as an online account or a leaderboard identity. It is not the device serial number, and the serial number cannot be derived from it. Uninstalling and reinstalling does not change it.

Width greater than height is landscape. When `display.orientation` is `portrait` or `landscape`, these fields do not change during the session. When it is `system`, rotation happens only between callbacks: the next callback sees the new width, height, orientation, and `occlusion`, and a redraw is already scheduled. The origin is the top left of the logical screen, x increases to the right, y increases downward. Pointer coordinates are already converted for the rotation.

Pixels inside `occlusion` are drawn as usual. They are just not visible. Put text, strokes, focus, and hit targets in the visible area.

## Gray levels

The host maps a color onto `gray_levels` steps. The step is `(color * gray_levels) // 16`. Step 0 is the lightest.

An e-ink panel needs a dedicated grayscale waveform and a full refresh (the whole screen flashes) before it can show intermediate gray. An app frame uses the fast refresh, which is black and white only, so every current profile has `gray_levels` of 2. How many gray steps the panel itself can show is a separate fact.

- When `gray_levels` is 2, `0..7` is drawn as paper and `8..15` is drawn as ink. Use `g:pattern` for a middle tone (section 6).
- Antialiasing on the edge of TTF text may use more steps of the panel. This limit does not apply to that.

Body text and controls use `0` and `15`. The result is the same on every device.

## Device profiles

| `model` | Portrait | Touch | Built-in keys | Gray levels | small / medium / large | Timer wake | Front light | Portrait occlusion top/right/bottom/left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x4_pro` | 480×800 | yes | `up` `down` `back` | 2 | 20 / 24 / 30 | yes | yes, warmth is adjustable | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `x4_classic` | 480×800 | no | `up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` `back` | 2 | 20 / 24 / 30 | yes | no | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |

A type size is the line height in pixels. A new profile may only add a row to this table, and the row must fill every column.

Every profile has a touchscreen, or it has `up`, `down`, and `ok` together, so the UI library in section 16 can be operated on every profile. The largest system font is 40 px. Larger type (clock digits and the like) uses TTF (section 7; put `ttf` in `requires`).

ctx.device.model          -- device profile name, see the table below
ctx.device.lock_timer     -- whether a timer can wake the lock screen (the "timer wake" column), boolean
ctx.device.name           -- 2.1: the name the user gave the device
ctx.device.firmware       -- 2.1: firmware version string
ctx.device.id_for_app     -- 2.1: a device id that differs per app

entries.content:
# 4. Input

```lua
ctx.input.keys      -- { up, down, left, right, ok, back }, each a boolean
ctx.input.pointer   -- true when there is a touchscreen
```

Both tables are written at the start of every callback. `back` is always true. A key built into the device is always true. While a Bluetooth page turner is connected, `up` and `down` are true, and its previous-page and next-page controls are delivered as `up` and `down`. A key that is false produces no events. The power key produces no events.

## Keys

```lua
{ type = "key", key = "ok", phase = "down", time_ms = 0 }
```

`phase` is `down` or `up`. One press is one pair. There is no auto-repeat. `time_ms` is the same counter as `ctx.clock:millis()`.

## Back

- **Short press** (held for less than 1000 ms): on release the host delivers `down` and then `up` for `back`, back to back. Only the return value of the `up` event matters: if it is not `true`, the app exits. The return value of the `down` event does nothing. Handle “go to the previous page” in `up`.
- **Long press** (held for 1000 ms): no event is delivered, and the app is forced to exit immediately. The running callback is cut off at the next Lua instruction, then `on_leave` is called. An app cannot intercept the long press.

The back area on a touchscreen is the same as the physical Back key. To go to the previous page, handle `back` and return `true`. On the outermost page return `false`, and the user is back in the system.

## Pointer

```lua
{ type = "pointer", phase = "up", x = 0, y = 0, time_ms = 0,
  down_x = 0, down_y = 0, gesture = "tap" }
```

Only one finger is tracked at a time. `x, y` is where this event happened.

| `phase` | When | Extra fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `down` | The finger goes down | |
| `move` | It moves while down. At least 4 px from the previous delivery, and at least 50 ms apart; if deliveries cannot keep up, only the latest position is delivered | `down_x` `down_y` |
| `hold` | Held for 700 ms, and both the horizontal and vertical distance from the down point are under 20 px. At most once per press | `down_x` `down_y` |
| `up` | The finger lifts | `down_x` `down_y` `gesture` |
| `cancel` | The system takes over. There is no `up` for this press after that | |

`gesture` on `up` is decided in order. The first match stops the search. Displacement is the `up` point minus the down point:

| Order | gesture | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `long` | This press delivered a `hold` |
| 2 | `swipe_right` / `swipe_left` | The absolute horizontal displacement is ≥ 50, and it is not smaller than the absolute vertical displacement |
| 3 | `swipe_down` / `swipe_up` | The absolute vertical displacement is ≥ 50, and it is greater than the absolute horizontal displacement |
| 4 | `double_tap` | It would have been a `tap`; the previous `up` was a `tap`; the two downs are at most 300 ms apart, and both the horizontal and vertical distance between the down points are under 20 px |
| 5 | `tap` | Everything else |

The press before a `double_tap` was already delivered as a `tap`. An app that only wants a single tap handles `tap`. Handle `hold` when a long press needs feedback at once.

## Text input

```lua
ctx.input:text({ title = "Search", text = "", max_bytes = 64, secret = false }, function(ctx, text)
  if text then query = text; ctx:invalidate() end
end)
```

After the current callback returns, the host opens the system text-input screen above the app (an on-screen keyboard on a device with touch, otherwise key-based character picking). The app receives `on_pause`. After the user confirms or cancels, the app receives `on_resume`, then the completion function is called once as a callback: on confirm, `text` is the string that was entered; on cancel (Back) it is nil. While the input screen is open, the app receives no input events.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | The caption above the field. Valid UTF-8, at most 64 bytes. May be omitted |
| `text` | Initial content. Valid UTF-8, no longer than `max_bytes`. Defaults to the empty string |
| `max_bytes` | Integer 1–256, default 64. The returned string is no longer than this many bytes |
| `secret` | Boolean. When true the field shows `*`. Default false |

Which characters can be entered is decided by the host input method. At least the printable ASCII range (`0x20`–`0x7E`) is included. The returned string is valid UTF-8. Confirming after the user clears the field yields `""`.

It returns nothing. A value outside the rules returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A previous input, or (2.1) a dialog, that has not finished returns `nil, "busy"`. A lock-screen session returns `nil, "inactive"`. An unfinished input is cancelled when the session ends, and the completion function is not called.
entries.example:
ctx.input.keys      -- { up, down, left, right, ok, back }, each a boolean
ctx.input.pointer   -- true when there is a touchscreen

entries.content:
# 5. Presenting a frame

```lua
ctx:invalidate()
ctx:invalidate("full")
ctx:defer_full_refresh(ms)
ctx.perf:info()
```

`invalidate` asks for one frame to be drawn and presented after the current callback returns. It returns nothing. Called from `on_draw`, it is queued for the next frame, and the waveform counts toward that next frame (a lock-screen session is the exception; see section 15). The argument is the waveform: omitted means a partial refresh; `"full"` is a full refresh, which clears ghosting and flashes once. If one frame is requested more than once, a single `"full"` makes the whole frame a full refresh. Any other argument returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

Every so many partial refreshes, the system inserts a full refresh on its own. The count is the one the user picked in system settings (often 6 to 30; Gancao firmware defaults to 30, so after 29 partial refreshes the 30th frame is a full refresh). A full refresh takes much longer than a partial one (about 1.5 seconds on the Gancao X4 Pro / X4 Classic, against about 0.65 seconds), so a continuous animation shows a pause there. `defer_full_refresh(ms)` makes presentations during the next `ms` milliseconds neither trigger nor count toward that automatic full refresh. Use it while paging or dragging so the screen does not flash. `ms` is an integer from 1 to 60000. It returns nothing. A later call replaces the deadline. `invalidate("full")` is not affected.

One frame accepts at most 1024 drawing commands. Each line `g:text_box` draws counts as one. The call that would exceed the limit returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"` and is not added to this frame. Commands already accepted stay.

`ctx.perf:info()` returns a table. Every field is an integer greater than or equal to 0. A field for something that has not happened yet is 0:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `tick_us` | Microseconds of the latest `on_tick` |
| `draw_us` | Microseconds of the latest `on_draw` |
| `cmd_count` | Commands accepted by the latest frame |
| `image_count` | How many times `g:image` ran in the latest frame |
| `asset_hit` `asset_miss` | Image-cache hits and misses, accumulated for the session |
| `draw_frame` | Frames completed |
entries.example:
ctx:invalidate()
ctx:invalidate("full")
ctx:defer_full_refresh(ms)
ctx.perf:info()

entries.content:
# 6. Drawing

The canvas `g` appears only as a parameter: the second parameter of `on_draw(ctx, g)`, and the parameter of `layer:draw(function(g) end)`. The canvas is valid only during that call. Using it afterwards makes every call return `nil, "inactive"`.

```lua
g:size()                                  -- width, height
g:clear(color)                            -- color defaults to 0
g:line(x0, y0, x1, y1, opts)
g:rect(x, y, w, h, opts)
g:circle(cx, cy, r, opts)
g:arc(cx, cy, r, start_deg, end_deg, opts)
g:polyline(points, opts)
g:polygon(points, opts)
g:pattern(x, y, w, h, opts)               -- optional capability pattern
g:text(x, y, text, opts)                  -- section 7
g:text_box(x, y, w, h, text, opts)        -- section 7
g:image(image, x, y, opts)
```

Success returns nothing.

## Style

| Field | Used by | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | all | 0..15 | 15 |
| `fill` | `rect` `circle` `polygon` | boolean | false, stroke only |
| `line_width` | strokes, `line`, `arc`, `polyline` | 1–255 | 1 |
| `radius` | `rect` | 0–255 | 0 |

`points` is a flat coordinate array `{ x1, y1, x2, y2, ... }`: `polyline` takes 2 to 128 points, `polygon` takes 3 to 128 points. The wrong count, or an odd length, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. `r` is an integer from 0 to 32767. `start_deg` and `end_deg` are integer degrees. 0 degrees is due right, and clockwise is positive. When the two differ by an integer multiple of 360, nothing is drawn.

## Pixel rules

The center of pixel `(px, py)` is `(px + 0.5, py + 0.5)`.

| Call | Pixels covered |
| --- | --- |
| `rect` fill | `[x, x+w) × [y, y+h)`. Nothing is drawn when `w` or `h` is not greater than 0 |
| `rect` stroke | The band inside the filled area whose distance to the outer edge is less than `line_width`. It grows inward only |
| `rect` with `radius` | The four corners are clipped to a circle: row `dy` (counting from 0) insets by `r - round(sqrt(r^2 - (r - dy - 0.5)^2))`. A `radius` past half the short side is treated as half the short side |
| `circle` fill | Distance from the center to `(cx + 0.5, cy + 0.5)` is less than `r` |
| `circle` stroke | The filled area whose distance is not less than `r - line_width` |
| `arc` | The part of a `circle` stroke from `start_deg` clockwise to `end_deg` |
| `line` | When `line_width` is 1, Bresenham, and both ends are drawn. When thicker, pixels whose distance to the segment is less than `line_width / 2` |
| `polyline` | `line` between adjacent points, in order. An overlap is drawn once |
| `polygon` fill | Pixels whose center is inside the polygon, by the even-odd rule. The first and last points are closed automatically |
| `polygon` stroke | The same as `polyline`, plus the last point back to the first |

## Patterns

When `ctx.capabilities.pattern` is true, `g.pattern` exists. Otherwise it is nil. `opts.kind` is `dot`, `line`, or `cross`, default `dot`. `opts.density` is an integer from 0 to 100, default 50, the percentage of the area covered by ink. `opts.color` defaults to 15. A pattern is aligned to the canvas origin, so two adjacent blocks meet with no seam.

## Images

`image` is an object returned by `ctx.package:image` or `ctx.layers:create`. Any other value returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. An object that has been released returns `nil, "invalid_handle"`. Drawing a layer into itself returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

| Field | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `w` `h` | 1–4096. Scaling happens only when both are set, with nearest-neighbor sampling | the image's own size |
| `color` | 0..15. Only for a black-and-white image: ink dots are drawn in this color (tint an icon) | 15 |
| `invert` | boolean | false |
| `background` | 0..15. When set, the destination rectangle is filled with it first, then the image is drawn | no fill |
| `radius` | 0–255, clips the output to rounded corners | 0 |

**Transparency comes from the asset itself**, the same way as PNG:

- The asset carries transparency (the PNG before packaging had an alpha channel): transparent pixels are not drawn, and what is already on the canvas stays. Opaque pixels are drawn as usual, and white is drawn as white.
- The asset carries no transparency: the whole image is opaque, and white covers whatever is underneath.
- A partly transparent pixel: on a device whose `gray_levels` is 2, opacity of at least 50% is drawn and less than that is not. A device with more gray levels uses the same 50% test. There is no blending.

Per pixel: look at transparency first. An opaque pixel takes the source color (an ink dot of a black-and-white image is `color`, a paper dot is 0; a grayscale image uses its own color). `invert` takes `15 - color`, then the gray-level mapping in section 3 is applied. `invert` does not change transparency.

When `ctx.capabilities.image_transform` is true, `flip_x` and `flip_y` (booleans), `rotate` (integer degrees, clockwise, modulo 360), `pivot_x`, and `pivot_y` (relative to the top left of the destination rectangle, default the rectangle's center) may also be set. The order is scale, flip, rotate, with nearest-neighbor sampling. When every field is at its default, the pixels match a call that omits them. Without the capability, setting any of those fields returns `nil, "not_supported"` and draws nothing.
entries.example:
g:size()                                  -- width, height
g:clear(color)                            -- color defaults to 0
g:line(x0, y0, x1, y1, opts)
g:rect(x, y, w, h, opts)
g:circle(cx, cy, r, opts)
g:arc(cx, cy, r, start_deg, end_deg, opts)
g:polyline(points, opts)
g:polygon(points, opts)
g:pattern(x, y, w, h, opts)               -- optional capability pattern
g:text(x, y, text, opts)                  -- section 7
g:text_box(x, y, w, h, text, opts)        -- section 7
g:image(image, x, y, opts)

entries.content:
# 7. Text and fonts

```lua
g:text(x, y, text, opts)
g:text_box(x, y, w, h, text, opts)

local font = ctx.fonts.medium                  -- small / medium / large
local names, err = ctx.fonts:installed()       -- optional capability ttf
local font, err = ctx.fonts:open(name, px)     -- optional capability ttf

font.name
font.line_height
font.ascent
local width = font:measure(text)
local lines, height, consumed = font:layout(text, w, h, opts)
```

## Text options

`text` must be a valid UTF-8 string, or the call returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Length limits: `g:text`, `g:text_box`, and `font:measure` take 8192 bytes each call, and all text in one frame totals 65536 bytes. `font:layout` takes 65536 bytes each call. Past that, the call returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. 8192 bytes is enough to fill a whole screen on any device.

| Field | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font` | a font object | `ctx.fonts.medium` |
| `color` | 0..15 | 15 |
| `align` | `left` `center` `right`; 2.1 also has `justify` | `left` |
| `valign` | `top` `middle` `baseline` `bottom` | `top` |
| `wrap` | `word` `char` `none` | `word`, only for `text_box` and `layout` |
| `overflow` | `clip` `ellipsis` `visible` | `clip`, only for `text_box` and `layout` |
| `line_gap` | 0–255 | 0, only for `text_box` and `layout` |

## Characters

- Code points are laid out left to right. There is no bidirectional reordering and no ligation. A string that contains a right-to-left character (Arabic, Hebrew, and the like) returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- A character the font does not have is drawn as a missing-glyph box, and the width is the width of that box.
- `\t` is one space. `\n` is not drawn by `g:text` or `measure`, and its width is 0. In `text_box` and `layout` it is a forced line break. Other control characters are not drawn, and their width is 0.

## Line box and alignment

One line of text occupies one line box. The width is `font:measure(text)`. The height is `font.line_height`. The baseline is `font.ascent` pixels below the top of the line box. Alignment looks at the line box, not at the ink, so different strings in the same font share a baseline when they share an anchor.

The baseline of a system font is placed so the ink of capital Latin letters, digits, and CJK characters sits vertically centered in the line box (within 1 pixel). That is why `valign = "middle"`, vertical centering in `text_box`, and the label inside a button look centered. The descenders of lowercase letters (g, y, p) fall below the midline. On `x4_pro` and `x4_classic`, `ascent` of `small`, `medium`, and `large` is 17, 21, and 26.

`(x, y)` of `g:text` is the anchor. `align` puts `x` at the left end, the midpoint, or the right end of the line box. `valign` puts `y` at the top, the vertical midpoint, the baseline, or the bottom of the line box. When centered, the left end of the line box is `x - width // 2`. When vertically centered, the top of the line box is `y - line_height // 2`.

## Text box

`g:text_box` lays text out inside a rectangle:

- `word` breaks at whitespace and between CJK characters, and does not split a Latin word. A word wider than the rectangle breaks at a code point. `char` breaks only at code points. `none` breaks only at `\n`. Whitespace at the start and end of a line takes no width.
- Each line is aligned horizontally to the rectangle width. The block of lines is aligned vertically to the rectangle height (`baseline` is treated as `top`).
- `justify` (2.1) justifies both ends: except for the last line of each paragraph (what follows is `\n` or the end of the text) and a line that has an ellipsis, the width left in the line is shared evenly between words (at the spaces). When there are no spaces, it is shared between CJK characters. A line with a single word is treated as `left`. `g:text` treats `justify` as `left`. `layout` is not affected. The block height is `n * line_height + (n - 1) * line_gap`.
- `clip` draws only whole lines that fit. `ellipsis`, when the text does not fit, draws `…` at the end of the last line that fits (or `...` if the font has no `…`), dropping characters from the end of that line if needed. `visible` draws every line, with no height limit.
- A line that cannot wrap (`wrap` is `none`, or one word is wider than the rectangle) and runs past the width: `clip` cuts off the overflow, `ellipsis` shortens it and ends with `…`, `visible` draws it anyway.
- When not even one line fits, nothing is drawn, and the call still succeeds.

## Measurement and paging

`font:measure(text)` returns the width of a single line. `font:layout(text, w, h, opts)` lays the text out by the rules of `text_box` but does not draw. It returns three integers: the number of lines drawn, the block height of those lines, and how many bytes fit. When the bytes that fit are less than `#text`, `text:sub(consumed + 1)` is the start of the next page: a newline at the end of the page, and a space where a line wrapped, count as part of this page, so the next page does not skip them again. `consumed` is always on a code-point boundary. When the text is longer than the per-call byte limit, use the standard-library `utf8.offset` to find a code-point boundary and split there. `layout` reads only `wrap`, `overflow`, and `line_gap`.

Neither call draws anything. Both may be called from any callback, and they do not count toward the command limit.

## Fonts

`ctx.fonts.small`, `medium`, and `large` are the system fonts. Line heights are in section 3. A size whose face has no CJK (for example `small` on `x4_pro`) switches drawing and measurement to `medium` when the string contains a CJK code point.

`font.name` is the system-font size name (`"small"` and so on) or the TTF name (the one from `installed`). A TTF font also has `font.px`, the size it was opened at.

When the face switches to `medium`, the whole string is laid out as `medium`: line height, baseline, and the height `layout` returns are those of `medium`. `font.line_height` and `font.ascent` stay the values of this size.

When `ctx.capabilities.ttf` is true, `installed` and `open` exist. Otherwise they are nil:

- `installed()` returns the TTF names available on the device, sorted by name, with no path and no `.ttf`. If they cannot be read, it returns `nil, "io_error"`.
- `open(name, px)`: `name` comes from `installed`. `px` is an integer from 8 to 96, the type size. Line height is decided by the font and is `font.line_height` (usually a little larger than `px`). The same pair returns the same object. The 33rd distinct pair returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. A missing file is `nil, "not_found"`. A face that does not fit in `ttf_reserve_kb` is `nil, "out_of_memory"`. A failed read is `nil, "io_error"`.

Every font object is used the same way, passed as `opts.font`.
entries.example:
g:text(x, y, text, opts)
g:text_box(x, y, w, h, text, opts)

local font = ctx.fonts.medium                  -- small / medium / large
local names, err = ctx.fonts:installed()       -- optional capability ttf
local font, err = ctx.fonts:open(name, px)     -- optional capability ttf

font.name
font.line_height
font.ascent
local width = font:measure(text)
local lines, height, consumed = font:layout(text, w, h, opts)

entries.content:
# 8. Packaged resources

```lua
local image, err = ctx.package:image(key)
image.width, image.height
image:release()
ctx.package:cache_stats()
ctx.package:exists(name)
ctx.package:size(name)
ctx.package:read(name)
local reader, err = ctx.package:open_text(name, opts)
```

`key` and `name` are file names. They must not contain `/` or `..`, or the call returns `nil, "invalid_argument"` (`exists` returns false).

**Images.** A packaged image is XIC, converted by the packager from PNG and the like: black and white, 4 levels, or 16 levels, with or without transparency (the packager keeps the source image's alpha channel). `image` returns an object. The same `key` returns the same object. A key not in the package is `nil, "not_found"`. A decode failure is `nil, "io_error"`. Not enough memory is `nil, "out_of_memory"`. The host keeps at most 320 decoded images at once, 524288 bytes in total. Past that it drops the one that has gone longest without being drawn (images drawn this frame or the previous frame are not dropped, so everything drawn in one frame is shown, even if the total exceeds 524288 bytes). A dropped object is decoded again the next time it is drawn, and that is invisible to the script. If decoding runs out of memory, the host drops images that are not on screen and tries once more. If that is still not enough, it returns `out_of_memory`. `release` drops the image on purpose, returns true, and may be called again. The object can still be asked for its width and height, and it can still be drawn.

`cache_stats()` returns `{ count, limit, bytes }`: how many images are cached, the limit 320, and the total bytes.

**Runtime images** (2.1): `ctx.image:decode`, `ctx.qr:encode`, and `ctx.reader:cover` also return image objects. They are used the same way, but they are not in the cache above. A session holds at most 8 of them at once, 524288 bytes in total. Asking for another returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. The host does not drop them. `release` frees the memory. After that, `g:image` of that object returns `nil, "invalid_handle"` (width and height can still be read). They are all released when the session ends.

**Data files.** `exists`, `size`, and `read` look only at `data_files`. A name not on that list makes `size` and `read` return `nil, "not_found"`. `read` returns the whole file as a byte string. A failed read is `nil, "io_error"`. Not enough memory is `nil, "out_of_memory"`. Read a large file line by line with `open_text`.

**Line by line.** `open_text` accepts only a listed file whose name ends in `.txt` or `.tsv`. `opts.max_line_bytes` defaults to 512 and is at most 65536.

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `reader:read_line()` | The next line, with a trailing `\n` and `\r` removed. nil at the end of the file. A line that is too long returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"` and skips to the next line |
| `reader:seek(pos)` | Moves to byte `pos` and returns true. A `pos` outside `0..file length` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"` |
| `reader:tell()` | The current byte position |
| `reader:close()` | Returns nothing, and may be called again. After that the first three methods return `nil, "invalid_handle"` |

## Messages

```lua
ctx.i18n.locale
ctx.i18n:t(key, params)
```

`locale` is the system UI language. It does not change during the session:

`zh` `zh-TW` `en` `ja` `ko` `tr` `de` `fr` `es` `it` `pt` `nl` `ru` `pl` `cs` `hu` `vi` `ms` `id` `th` `el` `bo` `sv` `ar`

Message files are `lang/<locale>.tsv` inside the package. They are not listed in `data_files`. Each line is `key<TAB>value`. A BOM, an empty line, a line with no TAB, and a line that starts with `#` are ignored. The two characters `\n` in a value mean a newline.

`t` looks up `lang/<locale>.tsv`, then (for `zh-TW`) `lang/zh.tsv`, then `lang/en.tsv`. If none of them has the key, it uses `key` itself. `params` may be omitted. When it is present, `{name}` in the value is replaced with `tostring(params.name)`. A name that is not in the table is left as written. A `key` that is not a string raises a Lua error. `t` does not return an error code.

```lua
ctx.i18n:t("greeting", { name = "Ada" })   -- greeting	Hello, {name}
```
entries.example:
local image, err = ctx.package:image(key)
image.width, image.height
image:release()
ctx.package:cache_stats()
ctx.package:exists(name)
ctx.package:size(name)
ctx.package:read(name)
local reader, err = ctx.package:open_text(name, opts)

entries.content:
# 9. Private files

This is the only persistence. No permission is required. Each app has its own directory, and other apps cannot see it. The main program and the lock screen share it. Uninstall deletes it.

```lua
ctx.storage:read(name)
ctx.storage:write(name, data)
ctx.storage:remove(name)
ctx.storage:exists(name)
ctx.storage:size(name)
ctx.storage:list()
ctx.storage:usage()
```

A name is 1–64 bytes, character set `[a-z0-9._-]`, and does not start or end with `.`. An illegal name returns `nil, "invalid_argument"` (`exists` returns false). `data` is a string and may contain any bytes.

Quota: one file is at most 262144 bytes, there are at most 512 files, and the total is at most 134217728 bytes (128 MB, exactly 512 full files). A `write` that would exceed any of those returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`, and the previous file is unchanged. A failed read or write, a missing card, or a card without enough free space returns `nil, "io_error"`. The quota is a ceiling, not a reservation: when the card is nearly full, a write can fail before the quota is reached.

| Call | File exists | File is absent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | the byte string | `nil, "not_found"` |
| `write` | replaces the whole file, returns true | creates it, returns true |
| `remove` | deletes it, returns true | returns true |
| `exists` | true | false |
| `size` | the byte count | `nil, "not_found"` |

`list()` returns an array sorted by the byte order of the names. `usage()` returns `{ files, bytes, max_files, max_bytes }`.

If power fails during `write`, a later read sees either the whole old content or the whole new content.

Reading and writing the storage card is slow, and the time counts against the limit of the current callback. Reference values measured on Gancao firmware (4 KB file, not guarantees): on the X4 Pro a write takes about 120 ms, a read about 35 ms, a remove about 70 ms; on the X4 Classic about 30 ms, 8 ms and 13 ms. On the X4 Pro, writing ten files in one callback already exceeds the 1000 ms limit. Combine the data you save into one file; if you really need to write many files, spread them over several `ctx:after` callbacks, a few at a time. Do not write files on every frame in `on_tick` or `on_draw`.

Store tables as JSON from section 10.
entries.example:
ctx.storage:read(name)
ctx.storage:write(name, data)
ctx.storage:remove(name)
ctx.storage:exists(name)
ctx.storage:size(name)
ctx.storage:list()
ctx.storage:usage()

entries.content:
# 10. JSON

```lua
local s, err = ctx.json:encode(value)
local value, err = ctx.json:decode(s)
ctx.json.null
```

**encode** accepts booleans, numbers, strings, and tables, and does not accept nil. Table rules:

- Keys that are exactly the contiguous integers `1..n` (or an empty table) encode as an array. Keys that are all strings encode as an object. A mix returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- `ctx.json.null` encodes as `null`.
- A function, coroutine, object, cyclic reference, nesting deeper than 32, NaN, or infinity returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- Object keys are written in byte order. A float uses the shortest decimal that restores that single-precision value. The result is at most 262144 bytes; otherwise `nil, "limit_exceeded"`.

**decode** returns the matching Lua value: an array becomes a table with keys `1..n`, an object becomes a table with string keys, and `null` becomes `ctx.json.null`. An integer that fits in 32 bits is an integer; otherwise it is a float. Input that is not valid JSON, or nesting deeper than 32, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

Encoding and decoding time counts against the limit of the current callback. Reference values measured on Gancao firmware (not guarantees): about 1.6 µs per byte (X4 Pro) and 2.2 µs (X4 Classic); encoding and then decoding 200 small records (four fields each) takes about 35 ms and 47 ms. Encode or decode large data once when you need it, not on every frame.
entries.example:
local s, err = ctx.json:encode(value)
local value, err = ctx.json:decode(s)
ctx.json.null

entries.content:
# 11. Offscreen layers

```lua
local layer, err = ctx.layers:create(w, h)
layer.width, layer.height
layer:draw(function(g) end)
g:image(layer, x, y, opts)
layer:release()
```

`w` and `h` are integers from 1 to `max(ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height)`. The buffer is `w * h` pixels. Each pixel is a `gray_levels` color plus 1 bit of transparency. A new layer is fully transparent. At most 4 exist at once. The 5th returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. Not enough memory returns `nil, "out_of_memory"`.

`draw` calls the function immediately and passes the layer's canvas. The origin is the layer's top left. Every drawing call from sections 6 and 7 is available. They draw straight into the buffer and do not count toward the per-frame command limit. `draw` may be called from any callback, to prepare content ahead of time. It cannot nest (calling it from another `draw` or from `on_draw` returns `nil, "busy"`). An error inside the function propagates as it is, and the buffer keeps the pixels from before the call. Success returns nothing.

`release` returns true and may be called again. After that, `draw` and a `g:image` that uses the layer as its source return `nil, "invalid_handle"`.

Blit it back to the screen, or onto another layer, with `g:image`. A layer carries its own transparency: a new layer is fully transparent, a pixel that has been drawn becomes opaque, and `g:clear(color)` makes the whole layer that opaque color.
entries.example:
local layer, err = ctx.layers:create(w, h)
layer.width, layer.height
layer:draw(function(g) end)
g:image(layer, x, y, opts)
layer:release()

entries.content:
# 12. Clock, log, and memory

```lua
ctx.clock:millis()
local t = ctx.clock:now()
ctx.log:info(msg)  ctx.log:warn(msg)  ctx.log:error(msg)
ctx.gc:collect()
ctx.gc:count()
```

`millis` returns milliseconds since this boot, in `0..2147483647`. After about 24.8 days it returns to 0. The gap between two samples is `(later - earlier) & 0x7FFFFFFF`, which stays correct across the wrap.

`now` returns a read-only table. Several calls in the same callback see the same snapshot.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `valid` | Whether the time may be shown to the user |
| `year` `month` `day` | Gregorian date. Month 1–12, day 1–31 |
| `hour` `minute` `second` | 0–23, 0–59, 0–59 |
| `weekday` | 0 is Sunday |
| `hour12` | Whether the system displays a 12-hour clock. It does not change `hour` |
| `offset_minutes` | Minutes from UTC, including daylight saving |
| `epoch_sec` | UTC Unix seconds. nil when it does not fit in a 32-bit integer (after 2038-01-19) |
| `local_sec` | `epoch_sec + offset_minutes * 60`. nil when it is out of range |
| `revision` | Increments when the time is set again, or the time zone or the 12/24-hour mode changes. 1 at the start of the session |

When `valid` is false, the date, the clock time, `weekday`, `epoch_sec`, and `local_sec` are nil. `valid`, `hour12`, `offset_minutes`, and `revision` always have a value.

There is no event for a time change. A clock face compares `revision` each time it wakes, and realigns when it changed. To land on the next minute: `ctx:after((60 - t.second) * 1000, fn)`, then read `now()` again on waking, because the wake can be a few hundred milliseconds late.

The three `log` methods take one string and return nothing. A non-string raises a Lua error. A log line may be dropped when space runs out. That is not an error.

`collect` runs one full collection. `count` returns how many bytes the script heap currently occupies.
entries.example:
ctx.clock:millis()
local t = ctx.clock:now()
ctx.log:info(msg)  ctx.log:warn(msg)  ctx.log:error(msg)
ctx.gc:collect()
ctx.gc:count()
