# 13. Device status

```lua
local b = ctx.device:battery()   -- { percent, charging }
local r = ctx.device:radios()    -- { wifi_on, wifi_connected, bluetooth_on }
```

No permission is required. `percent` is an integer 0–100, or -1 when it cannot be read. `charging` is a boolean, or false when it cannot be read. The three fields of `radios` are booleans.

2.1 also has: `voltage_mv` (battery voltage in millivolts) and `temperature_c` (battery temperature in degrees Celsius, an integer) on `battery()`, nil when they cannot be read. When the `net` permission is declared, `radios()` also has `wifi_ssid` (the network name) and `wifi_signal` (signal, 0–4 bars) while Wi-Fi is connected, and nil when it is not.
entries.example:
local b = ctx.device:battery()   -- { percent, charging }
local r = ctx.device:radios()    -- { wifi_on, wifi_connected, bluetooth_on }

entries.content:
# 14. Networking

Requires the `net` permission. When it is not declared, `ctx.net` is nil. It is also nil in a lock-screen session.

```lua
local job, err = ctx.net:request({
  url = "https://example.com/api",
  method = "POST",                 -- "GET" (the default) or "POST"
  headers = { ["content-type"] = "application/json" },
  body = ctx.json:encode({ q = 1 }),
}, function(ctx, res)
  if res.ok and res.status == 200 then
    data = ctx.json:decode(res.body)
    ctx:invalidate()
  end
end)
job:cancel()
```

**Request.**

- `url` starts with `http://` or `https://` and is at most 1024 bytes. https is checked with the device's built-in root certificates, so https fails when the clock is not valid (`io_error`).
- `body` is used only for `POST`. It is a string, at most 65536 bytes, default the empty string. A `GET` that sets `body` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- `headers` is a table of string to string, at most 16 items. A name is ≤ 64 bytes and a value is ≤ 1024 bytes. A `POST` that does not set `content-type` uses `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.
- Redirects are not followed. A 3xx is handed to the app as it is. `res.headers.location` is the target.
- When Wi-Fi is off but a network has been saved, the host turns it on and connects. The whole request has at most 30000 ms from the call: if Wi-Fi is not connected in that time, the result is `no_network`; if it connected and the response is still not complete, the result is `timeout`.

Only one request may be unfinished at a time. Another `request` returns `nil, "busy"`. An illegal argument returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Success returns the request object.

When `ok` is true, `status`, `headers`, `body`, and `bytes` all have values. When https fails and `ctx.clock:now().valid` is false, the clock is usually not set. Tell the user to go online and set the time first.

The **completion function** is called once as a callback after the request ends. The arguments are `ctx` and the result table:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | true when a complete HTTP response was received (any status code) |
| `status` | The status code. nil when no response was received |
| `headers` | Response headers, names lowercased. The same name is joined with `, `. At most 32 items, 4096 bytes in total |
| `body` | The response body, at most 131072 bytes kept |
| `bytes` | The total body size in bytes, including the part that was cut off |
| `err` | See the table below |

| `err` | When |
| --- | --- |
| nil | Success |
| `no_network` | No saved Wi-Fi, or it did not connect within 30000 ms |
| `timeout` | After connecting, 30000 ms from the call passed before the response was complete |
| `io_error` | The connection dropped, DNS or TLS failed, or the host cannot start a request right now |
| `limit_exceeded` | The body was longer than 131072 bytes and was cut off. `ok` is still true |

`job:cancel()` cancels an unfinished request. The completion function is not called. It returns nothing. It has no effect on a request that has already ended. An unfinished request is cancelled automatically when the session ends.
entries.example:
local job, err = ctx.net:request({
  url = "https://example.com/api",
  method = "POST",                 -- "GET" (the default) or "POST"
  headers = { ["content-type"] = "application/json" },
  body = ctx.json:encode({ q = 1 }),
}, function(ctx, res)
  if res.ok and res.status == 200 then
    data = ctx.json:decode(res.body)
    ctx:invalidate()
  end
end)
job:cancel()

entries.content:
# 15. Lock screen

An app can provide a lock-screen picture, refreshed on an interval while the device is locked (a clock, a calendar, a to-do list).

While locked, the device is in deep sleep and does not keep memory. Each refresh is therefore its own short session: load the lock-screen script, draw one frame, and end. The main program and the lock screen exchange data only through the files in section 9.

## Make this the lock screen

When the manifest has `lockscreen`, `ctx.lockscreen` exists in the main program. Otherwise it is nil:

```lua
ctx.lockscreen:set_default()
ctx.lockscreen:is_default()
```

`set_default` returns nothing. After the current callback returns, the host shows the system confirmation. The app receives `on_pause`, then `on_resume`. Inside `on_resume`, `is_default` is already the user's choice. If it is already the lock screen, no dialog is shown. The user can switch it back in system settings at any time. The app is not notified. Call `is_default` whenever the answer is needed.

## When it runs

Whether to lock, and when, is the system's decision (idle timeout or the power key). When the lock-screen app is this app:

1. If an app is in the foreground, end its session first (`on_leave`).
2. Run one lock-screen session. `ctx.lock.reason` is `"first"`.
3. Sleep until the next whole multiple of `interval_sec` (local time: an interval of 60 wakes on the minute). When the clock is not valid, sleep for `interval_sec` seconds.
4. Wake and run one lock-screen session. `reason` is `"timer"`. Go back to step 3.

A device with no timer wake does only step 2.

## One lock-screen session

`on_load(ctx)`, then `on_draw(ctx, g)`, then the host presents the frame and ends. The two callbacks together are at most 2000 ms, and that cannot be extended. Those are the only two callbacks. `ctx:after` and `ctx:set_tick` do nothing. `ctx.budget:extend()` returns `nil, "inactive"`.

The canvas starts as paper each time, and the callback draws a complete frame. The default is a full refresh for `first` and a partial refresh for `timer`. Calling `ctx:invalidate("full")` from `on_load` or `on_draw` changes it to a full refresh. The host keeps the count of consecutive partial refreshes in a record that survives sleep, and it still inserts the automatic full refresh.

`ctx` in a lock-screen session is the same as in the main program. `require` works as usual, and the screen orientation still follows `display.orientation` in the manifest. Only these differ: `ctx.lock` exists; `ctx.net` and `ctx.lockscreen` are nil; `ctx.input:text` returns `nil, "inactive"`; `ctx:after` and `ctx:set_tick` do nothing; `ctx.budget:extend()` returns `nil, "inactive"`. A device whose `ctx.device.lock_timer` is false runs only the `first` session.

In a timer wake (`reason` is `"timer"`), the host does not turn on Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, regardless of the user's switches: `wifi_on`, `wifi_connected`, and `bluetooth_on` from `ctx.device:radios()` are all false. After the user leaves the lock screen with the power key, the radios return to the user's settings. The `first` session is not affected.

```lua
ctx.lock.reason        -- "first" | "timer"
ctx.lock.elapsed_sec   -- seconds since the previous lock-screen present; 0 for first
ctx.lock.interval_sec  -- the current interval
ctx.lock:set_interval(seconds)
```

`ctx.lock` exists only in a lock-screen session. The argument of `set_interval` is an integer from 30 to 3600. It takes effect starting with the sleep after this session, and returns nothing. The next time the lock screen is entered, it starts again from the manifest value.

The session still runs when the clock is not valid. `ctx.clock:now().valid` is false, and the script decides what to draw.

## Exceptions

- If the lock-screen script errors or runs out of time, the host draws the system default lock-screen picture and stops timer wakes until the next time the lock screen is entered.
- Below 5% battery and not charging: the script does not run. The host draws the low-battery picture and powers off.
- The power key: leave the lock screen and return to the system. The app that was in the foreground before the lock screen opens again, as a brand-new session.
entries.example:
ctx.lockscreen:set_default()
ctx.lockscreen:is_default()

entries.content:
# 16. UI library

Optional capability `ui`: when it is true, `ctx.ui` exists. Otherwise it is nil. Immediate mode: every frame, declare the controls again inside `on_draw`. The library draws them, hit-tests them, and keeps focus.

```lua
local ui = ctx.ui:create()        -- create it once in on_load

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  ui:begin_frame(g)
  ui:label("title", { x = 20, y = 20, w = 440, h = 40, text = "Settings", font = ctx.fonts.large })
  ui:switch("wifi", { x = 20, y = 80, w = 440, h = 56, text = "Wi-Fi", selected = wifi })
  ui:button("save", { x = 20, y = 160, w = 200, h = 56, text = "Save", radius = 8 })
  ui:end_frame()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local id, action = ui:handle_event(ev)
  if action == "activate" then
    if id == "wifi" then wifi = not wifi end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if action then ctx:invalidate(); return true end
  return false
end
```

`begin_frame` returns `nil, "busy"` when the previous frame had no `end_frame`. `end_frame` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"` when there was no `begin_frame`. The library does not clear the screen. Call `g:clear()` yourself before `begin_frame`. Controls default to `ctx.fonts.medium` and color 15.

Each control's `id` is a non-empty string, and it cannot repeat in the same frame (a repeat returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`). `x`, `y`, `w`, and `h` are required. `w` and `h` are at least 1. More than 128 controls in one frame, or a container nested more than 16 deep, returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`, and that control is not drawn.

| Control | Fields | How it is drawn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `text` `font` `color` `align` `valign` | Drawn in the box as `text_box`, with `overflow` of `ellipsis` |
| `button` | `text` `font` `radius` | A stroked rounded box, text centered. When focus is drawn, the fill is 15 and the text is 0 |
| `switch` | `text` `font` `selected` | Text on the left, an `h × h` box on the right, filled when `selected`. When focus is drawn, the stroke is 2 |
| `image` | `source` | An image object scaled to `w × h` |
| `row` `column` | `gap` `children` | See below |

`children` of `row` and `column` is an array. Each item is `{ kind = "button", id = "...", w = ..., h = ..., ... }`, with no `x` or `y`. A `row` lays out left to right from its own `(x, y)`, tops aligned. A `column` lays out top to bottom, left edges aligned. Neighbors are separated by `gap` (default 0). Anything past the container is clipped.

**Hit testing**: the last `button` or `switch` added this frame that contains the point.

**Focus**: hittable controls are ordered by when they were added. Focus is kept across frames by `id`. If that `id` is absent this frame, focus falls on the first one. If nothing is hittable, focus is empty.

`handle_event(ev)` returns `id, action`. When there is no matching action it returns nil, nil:

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `down` of `ok` | The focused control, `press` |
| `up` of `ok`, and focus did not move | The focused control, `activate` |
| `down` of `up` / `left` | Focus moves to the previous one. `id` is the new focus, `action` is `focus` |
| `down` of `down` / `right` | Focus moves to the next one. Same as above |
| Pointer `tap` or `double_tap` | The hit control, `activate`. Focus moves to it |
| Pointer `hold` | The hit control, `long_press` |

An `ev` that is not an event table from section 4 returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A control does not store `selected`. The script passes it every frame. The library does not draw a pressed look. `press` only tells the script.

**Whether focus is drawn**: focus is drawn only while keys are driving it. A device with no touchscreen always draws it. A device with a touchscreen starts drawing it after a key event is given to `handle_event`, and stops drawing it after a pointer event is given to `handle_event` (the focus itself is kept, and the next key starts from it).

`double_tap` is the second tap: two quick taps on a button produce two `activate` results, and a switch is toggled twice.
entries.example:
local ui = ctx.ui:create()        -- create it once in on_load

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  ui:begin_frame(g)
  ui:label("title", { x = 20, y = 20, w = 440, h = 40, text = "Settings", font = ctx.fonts.large })
  ui:switch("wifi", { x = 20, y = 80, w = 440, h = 56, text = "Wi-Fi", selected = wifi })
  ui:button("save", { x = 20, y = 160, w = 200, h = 56, text = "Save", radius = 8 })
  ui:end_frame()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local id, action = ui:handle_event(ev)
  if action == "activate" then
    if id == "wifi" then wifi = not wifi end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if action then ctx:invalidate(); return true end
  return false
end

entries.content:
# 17. Optional capabilities

`ctx.capabilities` exists at the start of the session. Every field is a boolean, and it does not change during the session. The host may report any of the following as false.

| Field | Present when true | When false |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pattern` | `g:pattern` | `g.pattern` is nil |
| `image_transform` | Transform fields of `g:image` | Writing those fields returns `nil, "not_supported"` |
| `ttf` | `ctx.fonts:installed`, `ctx.fonts:open` | Both functions are nil |
| `ui` | `ctx.ui` | `ctx.ui` is nil |
| `reader` (2.1) | `ctx.reader` (also requires the `reader` permission) | `ctx.reader` is nil |
| `dialog` (2.1) | `ctx.dialog` | `ctx.dialog` is nil |
| `frontlight` (2.1) | `ctx.frontlight` | `ctx.frontlight` is nil |
| `image_decode` (2.1) | `ctx.image:decode` | `ctx.image` is nil |

The name of an optional capability is the name of its namespace (`image_decode` is the exception: the namespace is `ctx.image`). On a 2.0 host the 2.1 fields are absent (nil), so treat the capability as missing unless `ctx.capabilities.dialog` is true.

When the field is true, the corresponding calls behave as this document says and must not return `not_supported`. An app that cannot run without one lists it in manifest `requires`.

# 18. Error codes

The second return value of a call uses only these strings:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_argument` | The type is right, and the value is outside the stated range |
| `not_found` | Nothing exists for that name |
| `io_error` | A storage, decode, or network read or write failed |
| `out_of_memory` | The host could not allocate memory for this call |
| `busy` | The same kind of operation is already in progress |
| `invalid_handle` | The object has already been released or closed |
| `limit_exceeded` | A count or size stated in this document was exceeded |
| `inactive` | Not an allowed moment: the canvas has expired, `extend` was called outside a callback, or text input or a dialog was requested in a lock-screen session |
| `not_supported` | Returned only by `g:image` when `image_transform` is absent |

A network result's `err` may also be `no_network` or `timeout`. Those appear only in the result table in section 14.

# 19. Versions

`ctx.api` is `{ major = 2, minor = <the minor the host implements> }`.

A 2.x minor only adds: new calls, new optional capabilities, new device profiles, new `requires` names, new `locale` values, and new optional manifest fields. Parameters, return values, and error codes of existing calls do not change.

The host supports 2.m and the package says `"api": "2.n"`: `n <= m` installs and runs; `n > m` is refused at install, with a prompt to update the firmware. An incompatible change can only arrive in 3.0.

When the host also runs packages whose `api` is 0.x or 1.x, those packages follow their own older contracts. A 2.0 package sees none of the names from those older contracts.

**2.1** adds: sections 22–27; the manifest `permissions` name `reader`; the `requires` names `reader`, `dialog`, `frontlight`, and `image_decode`; `ctx.device.name`, `firmware`, and `id_for_app`; new fields of `battery()` and `radios()`; `align = "justify"`; runtime images (section 8). On a host that implements 2.1, `ctx.api.minor` is 1, and a 2.0 package can see these new names too. To stay installable on a 2.0 device, write `"2.0"` and test `ctx.api.minor >= 1` and `ctx.capabilities`.

# 20. Conformance tests

Each section has a set of test apps. The tests run on the host's simulator and on hardware. The log prints `api2 <section> passed checks=<n>`. Drawing results are compared pixel by pixel with the golden image for each device profile.

A host that claims to support 2.m must pass every test except section 17, and must pass the tests for every optional capability it reports as true. A rule with no test cannot enter a release.

# 21. Capability list

| Capability | Section |
| --- | --- |
| Bounded callbacks, extend by 11 seconds, 30 seconds at most | 2 |
| A tick on demand (`set_tick`) and a one-shot timer (`after`) | 2 |
| Pause and resume | 2 |
| Keys the device reports, down and up in pairs, Bluetooth page turner | 3, 4 |
| A short press of Back is delivered to the app; a long press forces an exit | 4 |
| Pointer down, move, hold, up, and cancel; tap, double-tap, long-press, and four-way swipe | 4 |
| System text input | 4 |
| Declare required input and capabilities at install | Manifest |
| Screen, orientation, gray levels, occlusion, device profile | 3 |
| Pixel-exact rectangles (including rounded), circles, arcs, lines, polylines, polygons, patterns | 6 |
| Image scale, invert, background fill, rounded clip, transforms | 6 |
| Text alignment (including the baseline), wrapping, ellipsis, measurement, paging | 7 |
| System fonts, device TTF | 7 |
| Packaged images, data files, line-by-line reading, message catalogs in 24 languages, and parameter substitution | 8 |
| Application private files, shared by the main program and the lock screen | 9 |
| JSON encode and decode | 10 |
| Offscreen layers the size of their arguments | 11 |
| Monotonic milliseconds, wall clock, log, garbage collection, frame measurements | 5, 12 |
| Battery, charging, radio state | 13 |
| Async GET and POST, http and https, response headers, completion callback, and cancel | 14 |
| Lock-screen frames refreshed on an interval | 15 |
| Immediate-mode UI library with focus | 16 |
| A minor version only adds | 19 |
| 2.1: recently read books, progress, reading time per day, totals, covers | 22 |
| 2.1: system confirm, choice, and toast | 23 |
| 2.1: temporary front-light change for this session | 24 |
| 2.1: open the system Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings | 25 |
| 2.1: base64, hexadecimal, URL encoding; SHA-256, SHA-1, MD5, HMAC, CRC-32; secure random bytes, UUID | 26 |
| 2.1: decompress gzip / zlib, generate a QR code, decode an image downloaded from the network | 27 |
| 2.1: justified text; device name, firmware version, per-app device id; battery voltage and temperature; Wi-Fi name and signal | 3, 7, 13 |

# 22. Reading data (2.1)

Requires the `reader` permission and the `reader` optional capability. Otherwise `ctx.reader` is nil. Both the main program and a lock-screen session may use it. It is read-only.

```lua
local books = ctx.reader:books()            -- recently read books, most recent first
local book  = ctx.reader:current()          -- the book being read, or the most recent; nil if there is none
local days  = ctx.reader:days("2026-10-05", "2026-10-11")
local sum   = ctx.reader:summary()
local cover, err = ctx.reader:cover(book.id)
```

**Books.** `books()` returns an array of at most 18 books, ordered by most recent reading. No books returns an empty table. `current()` is the book being read right now, otherwise the most recently read book, and nil if none has ever been read. Both return the same kind of table:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The book's id. An opaque string. Stable across sessions |
| `title` | Title |
| `author` | Author. `""` when unknown |
| `format` | `"epub"`, `"txt"`, or `"xtc"`. More may be added later |
| `percent` | Progress, an integer 0–100 |
| `page` `total_pages` | Page number and page count. nil before the book has been paginated |
| `finished` | Whether it has been finished |
| `read_sec` | Seconds spent reading this book, accumulated |

**Time per day.** The dates of `days(from, to)` are `"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings, both ends included, at most 366 days. It returns an array with one item per day, `{ date, sec }`. A day with no reading is still present, with `sec` 0. Week, month, and year totals, and bar charts, are computed from this array. A bad date format, a date that does not exist (such as 30 February), `from` later than `to`, or more than 366 days returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

**Totals.** `summary()` returns:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `total_sec` | Accumulated reading seconds |
| `today_sec` | Today's seconds. nil when the clock is not valid |
| `days_read` | Days on which something was read |
| `streak_days` `best_streak_days` | The current run of reading days, and the longest run |
| `books_finished` | Books finished |
| `first_date` | The date of the first reading record. nil when there is none |

**Cover.** `cover(id)` returns, synchronously, the cover already generated for this book (a runtime image, section 8). It does not open the book file. The host chooses the size. Scale it with `w` and `h` of `g:image` when drawing. An unknown `id`, or a book that does not have a generated cover yet (it has never been shown on the shelf), returns `nil, "not_found"`.

A failed read returns `nil, "io_error"`.
entries.example:
local books = ctx.reader:books()            -- recently read books, most recent first
local book  = ctx.reader:current()          -- the book being read, or the most recent; nil if there is none
local days  = ctx.reader:days("2026-10-05", "2026-10-11")
local sum   = ctx.reader:summary()
local cover, err = ctx.reader:cover(book.id)

# 23. System dialogs (2.1)

Optional capability `dialog`.

```lua
ctx.dialog:confirm({ title = "Delete the record", message = "This cannot be undone.", ok_text = "Delete" },
  function(ctx, ok) if ok then remove_record() end end)

ctx.dialog:choose({ title = "Sort", items = { "By time", "By name" }, selected = 1 },
  function(ctx, index) if index then sort_by = index; ctx:invalidate() end end)

ctx.dialog:toast("Saved")
```

`confirm` and `choose` behave like text input in section 4: after the current callback returns, the host opens the dialog and the app receives `on_pause`; after the user chooses, the app receives `on_resume`, then the completion function is called once as a callback. While the dialog is open the app receives no input events. Back means cancel.

| Call | Fields | Second argument of the completion function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `title` (≤ 95 bytes), `message` (≤ 191), `ok_text`, `cancel_text` (each ≤ 63; the defaults are the system's Confirm and Cancel) | true for confirm, false for cancel |
| `choose` | `title`, `items` (1–7 strings, each ≤ 63 bytes, required), `selected` (1-based row, may be omitted) | the selected row (1-based), or nil on cancel |

`toast(text)` shows one line on the screen for about 2 seconds. It does not interrupt the app and returns nothing. `text` is at most 47 bytes.

They return nothing. Text that is too long returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. An empty `items`, or a `selected` outside the list, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A dialog or a text input that has not finished returns `nil, "busy"`. A lock-screen session returns `nil, "inactive"`. An unfinished dialog is cancelled when the session ends, and the completion function is not called.

# 24. Front light (2.1)

Optional capability `frontlight`: `ctx.frontlight` exists when the device has a front light, otherwise it is nil. It is nil in a lock-screen session.

```lua
local f = ctx.frontlight:get()                       -- { on, brightness, warmth }
ctx.frontlight:set({ on = true, brightness = 20 })   -- write only the fields to change
ctx.frontlight:reset()                               -- back to the user's settings
```

`brightness` and `warmth` are integers 0–100 (`warmth` 0 is the coolest, 100 is the warmest). `set` lasts only for this session and does not change system settings. `get` returns the values the app set. When the session ends (including entering the lock screen) the host calls `reset` on its own. If the system's night mode is running, `reset` hands the front light back to night mode. On a device with no warm light, `warmth` is always 0, and writing it is ignored.

`set` and `reset` return nothing. A value outside the range returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

# 25. Opening a system page (2.1)

```lua
if not online and ctx.system:can_open("settings.wifi") then
  ctx.system:open("settings.wifi")
end
```

After the current callback returns, `open` ends this session (it calls `on_leave`) and opens a system page. When the user comes back from that page, the app opens again as a brand-new session. Work that must continue is written, in `on_leave`, into a file from section 9.

| Target | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `"settings.wifi"` | Wi-Fi settings |
| `"settings.bluetooth"` | Bluetooth settings |

Later minors only add targets. `can_open(target)` returns a boolean. An unknown target, and a lock-screen session, are false, and `open` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A successful `open` returns nothing.
entries.example:
if not online and ctx.system:can_open("settings.wifi") then
  ctx.system:open("settings.wifi")
end

entries.content:
# 26. Encoding, hashes, and random bytes (2.1)

Required. Arguments and results are byte strings.

```lua
ctx.base64:encode(s, opts)   ctx.base64:decode(s)
ctx.hex:encode(s)            ctx.hex:decode(s)
ctx.url:encode(s)            ctx.url:decode(s)
ctx.url:query(t)             -- { q = "eink", page = 2 } -> "page=2&q=eink"

ctx.hash:sha256(s)  ctx.hash:sha1(s)  ctx.hash:md5(s)
ctx.hash:hmac_sha256(key, s)
ctx.hash:crc32(s)

ctx.random:bytes(n)
ctx.random:uuid()
```

- **base64**: the RFC 4648 standard alphabet, padded with `=`. When `opts.url` is true, the alphabet is `-` `_` and there is no padding. `decode` accepts both alphabets, and padding may be omitted.
- **hex**: `encode` writes lowercase. `decode` accepts either case, and the length must be even.
- **url**: `encode` writes every byte outside `A–Z a–z 0–9 - . _ ~` as `%XX` (a space is `%20`). `decode` only undoes `%XX`. `+` stays as it is. The keys of `query(t)` must be strings, and the values strings, numbers, or booleans. It joins them in the byte order of the keys. Keys and values are both passed through `encode`. An empty table yields `""`. At most 64 items.
- **hash**: returns the raw digest bytes (SHA-256 is 32 bytes, SHA-1 is 20, MD5 is 16), the same as Python `hashlib` `digest()`. For hexadecimal, write `ctx.hex:encode(ctx.hash:sha256(s))`. `hmac_sha256` follows RFC 2104. `crc32` matches zlib `crc32`, but it is returned as a signed 32-bit integer (values above `0x7FFFFFFF` are negative).
- **random**: `bytes(n)` returns `n` hardware-random bytes. `n` is an integer 1–1024. `uuid()` returns a version-4 UUID string (lowercase, with `-`). Suited to tokens and random seeds. `math.random` is not.

Input is at most 1048576 bytes. Longer input returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. An illegal character or a wrong length while decoding returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Encryption and decryption are not provided.
entries.example:
ctx.base64:encode(s, opts)   ctx.base64:decode(s)
ctx.hex:encode(s)            ctx.hex:decode(s)
ctx.url:encode(s)            ctx.url:decode(s)
ctx.url:query(t)             -- { q = "eink", page = 2 } -> "page=2&q=eink"

ctx.hash:sha256(s)  ctx.hash:sha1(s)  ctx.hash:md5(s)
ctx.hash:hmac_sha256(key, s)
ctx.hash:crc32(s)

ctx.random:bytes(n)
ctx.random:uuid()

# 27. Decompression, QR codes, and image decode (2.1)

```lua
local text = ctx.zlib:decompress(res.body)                     -- recognizes gzip or zlib
local code = ctx.qr:encode("https://example.com/r/42", { size = 240 })
local img  = ctx.image:decode(res.body, { max_w = 96, max_h = 96 })   -- optional capability image_decode
```

**Decompression** (required). `opts.format` is `"auto"` (the default), `"gzip"`, `"zlib"`, or `"raw"` (bare deflate). gzip checks the CRC-32 and the length at the end. The result is at most 1048576 bytes. Longer output returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. Damaged data, or the wrong format, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Compression is not provided.

**QR codes** (required). Returns a black-and-white runtime image (section 8) with a white margin of 4 modules on every side. `opts.size` is the desired side in pixels (21–4096, default 200). The host picks the largest whole-number module size that does not exceed it. The actual side is `code.width`. `opts.ecc` is `"low"`, `"medium"` (the default), `"quartile"`, or `"high"`. The content is at most 1024 bytes and contains no `\0`. If it does not fit (too much content, or `size` smaller than the module count plus the white margin) the call returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`.

**Image decode** (optional capability `image_decode`). Decodes PNG, JPEG, or BMP bytes into a runtime image, dithers to the device gray levels, and scales uniformly to fit inside `max_w × max_h` (1–4096, default the screen size). It runs synchronously, and the time counts against the current callback. A source whose width or height exceeds 1024 returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. An unrecognized format returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Not enough memory returns `nil, "out_of_memory"`. Together with section 14: a response body keeps at most 131072 bytes, so a larger picture has to be reduced by the server first.
entries.example:
local text = ctx.zlib:decompress(res.body)                     -- recognizes gzip or zlib
local code = ctx.qr:encode("https://example.com/r/42", { size = 240 })
local img  = ctx.image:decode(res.body, { max_w = 96, max_h = 96 })   -- optional capability image_decode

# Appendix A Packaging

The app is handed to the packager as a source directory. The packager writes one `.xtapp` file.

```bash
python3 tools/lua_app_packager/pack.py my_app --out my_app.xtapp
```

## Source directory

```text
my_app/
├── manifest.json
├── index.lua            main program; other .lua files may live in subdirectories
├── lib/util.lua         require("lib.util")
├── assets/              images: .png or .xic
├── data/                data files, listed in manifest.data_files
└── lang/                messages: <locale>.tsv
```

- **Scripts**: every `.lua` in the directory (directories whose names start with `.` are excluded). A script name is a relative path, at most 95 bytes. `require("a.b")` loads `a/b.lua`.
- **Images**: `.png` and `.xic` under `assets/`. The key is the file name without the extension, at most 23 bytes, character set `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. A `.png` and a `.xic` with the same name fail the package.
- **Data files**: files under `data/` that are listed in `data_files`. A name is at most 64 bytes, character set `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, the extension matches `format` (`txt`, `tsv`, or `json`), and the file does not exceed `max_bytes`.
- **Messages**: `.tsv` under `lang/`. They are not declared. Each is at most 32 KB.

How to write `data_files`:

```json
"data_files": [
  { "name": "book.txt", "format": "txt", "max_bytes": 65536 },
  { "name": "cities.json", "format": "json", "max_bytes": 8192 }
]
```

## Message files

UTF-8 text, one `key<TAB>value` per line. A leading BOM and a trailing `\r` are removed. An empty line, a line that starts with `#`, and a line with no TAB are ignored. The value is everything after the first TAB, and the two characters `\n` in it mean a newline. When the same key appears more than once, the first one is kept. Substitution of `{name}` is in section 8.

## Image conversion

The packager turns PNG into XIC:

| What the PNG contains | XIC |
| --- | --- |
| Every visible pixel is pure black or pure white | black and white (1 bit) |
| Anything else | 16-level gray |
| Any pixel is not fully opaque | an extra 1 bit of transparency: a pixel whose opacity is at least 50% is opaque (the same rule as drawing in section 6, so nothing visible is lost), one extra bit per pixel |

Gray is `0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B`. For a black-and-white photograph, dither it to pure black and white in the drawing tool first, then save it. Only non-interlaced PNG is read. A file that is already `.xic` is packaged as it is (black and white, 4 levels, and 16 levels are all allowed).

## Icons and the splash image

| Manifest field | Suggested size | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app_icon_l` | 200 × 150 | The card in the app list. Falls back to `app_icon_s` |
| `app_icon_s` | 100 × 100 | The small icon |
| `splash` | at most 400 × 400 | Shown centered while `on_load` runs, as the app opens |

All three are keys in `assets/`, shown in black and white. The packager also puts them in the unencrypted part of the package, so the host can show them without unpacking the whole package.

## Limits

| Item | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `.xtapp` file | 32 MB |
| Scripts | 128 |
| Images | 2048 (320 decoded at once; see section 8) |
| Data files and message files together | 128 |
| A file `open_text` can open | 1 MB |

## Rules the packager checks

For a package whose `"api"` is `"2.x"`, the packager checks the following first. A failure is an error and no file is written: the character set and length of `app_id`, `display_name` and `version` non-empty, `entry` and `lockscreen.entry` present in the package, `requires` and `permissions` containing only names listed in this document (including the 2.1 names), keys of `preload_assets` and of the icons and splash present under `assets/`, the range of `ttf_reserve_kb`, the value of `display.orientation`, and every item of `data_files`. The host checks them again at install, and also checks whether `requires` is satisfied on this device.

# Appendix B Upgrading an app

- **Installing the same `app_id` again is an upgrade.** The package is replaced. Private files from section 9 are all kept. The host does not compare `version`. An older version can be installed again. Uninstall deletes the package and every private file.
- **`app_id` cannot change.** A different id is a different app. The old app's files are not moved across.
- **A save format carries a version.** For example `{ "v": 2, ... }`. When `on_load` reads an older version, convert it and write it back. When it reads a newer version it does not recognize (the user installed an older build again), do not overwrite it; run with defaults.
- **When a field is renamed, also read the old name.** Keep that for at least one version, then delete the compatibility code.
- **The lock-screen setting follows `app_id`.** After an upgrade it is still the lock screen. If the new version drops `lockscreen` from the manifest, the device draws the system default when it locks.
- **Using a newer minor:** after the manifest says `"api": "2.1"`, the package installs only on a device that supports 2.1 (section 19). To stay installable on an older device, keep `2.0` and use the optional capabilities in section 17 to see whether a new feature is there.

# Appendix C Wording and terms

## Normative wording

This document states rules in the indicative: “returns …”, “is nil”, and “refuses install” are behavior the host must implement, and an author may rely on it. “May” means allowed, not required. “Prefer” and “suited to” are advice about how to write, not rules. Behavior that is not written down cannot be relied on.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Host | The firmware or simulator that runs the app |
| Package | One `.xtapp` file, that is, one app |
| Session | One run from load to leave. When it ends, all memory is discarded (section 2) |
| Lock-screen session | A short session that runs the lock-screen script while the device is locked, draws one frame, and ends (section 15) |
| Callback | An app function the host calls: `on_*`, a timer function, or a completion function |
| Budget | The longest one callback may run (section 2) |
| Canvas | The `g` passed to `on_draw` and `layer:draw`. Valid only for that call |
| Frame | The full-screen picture one `on_draw` produces |
| Present | Send one frame to the panel |
| Partial refresh / full refresh | The two e-ink updates: a partial refresh is fast and does not flash, but leaves ghosting; a full refresh flashes once and clears the ghosting (section 5) |
| Color | An ink level from 0 to 15. 0 is paper, 15 is the blackest |
| Gray levels | How many shades the screen actually shows (section 3) |
| Device profile | The fixed screen, keys, touch, and type sizes of one class of device (section 3) |
| Optional capability | A group of features the host may omit (section 17) |
| Packaged resources | Images, data files, and message catalogs inside the package. Read-only (section 8) |
| Private files | Files the app itself can write. Kept across an upgrade (section 9) |
| Code point | One Unicode character. In UTF-8 it occupies 1 to 4 bytes |
| Line box | The rectangle one line of text occupies. The width is the measured width. The height is the line height (section 7) |

# Studio 预览桥

## 作用

用户在本地写 XTApp，打开一个官网预览页看效果，改本地代码后页面更新。Studio 是项目和 Lua Worker 的运行 authority。插件通过官网 `/preview/*` 排队命令。模拟器画面在官网预览页，不在 Codex 右侧 widget。

`run_xtapp_preview` 必须带当前 worktree 的绝对路径 `projectDir`。它会读取本机 Lua、Manifest、data、lang，以及 `assets|raw` 下 `.xic` 与 `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp`。单次 HTTP 会限制素材条数，插件会自动分批 `POST` 再 `PATCH` 合并，工程可以有更多素材。不要为了预览桥去删图、改字模或拆工程。官网会为这个 worktree **新建或复用独立项目**，不会覆盖用户正在写的其他工程（例如斗地主）。不要说插件不读文件系统。不要省略 `projectDir` 去跑官网里已经打开的项目。

所有 `/preview/*` JSON 都是信封：`{ok,data}` 或 `{ok,false,error:{code,message,details}}`。`ok` 只表示这次 HTTP 调用是否按契约完成。预览页没开时仍是 `ok: true`，`data.status: "not_connected"`。

## 启动

1. 调用 `run_xtapp_preview`，拿到带插件 session 的 `previewUrl`。不要只打开 `region.json` 里 `studioOrigin` 的裸 `/studio/preview?preview=1`。
2. 打开这条 URL，并保持打开。打开方式取决于宿主：
   - **有浏览器 MCP 的宿主（Cursor）：** 用内置浏览器 MCP（`browser_tabs` / `browser_navigate`）打开 `previewUrl`，不要请用户另开 Chrome。出现登录页就停下，请用户在这个内置页里登录，Agent 不填账号密码。登录后再回到同一条 `previewUrl`。
   - **其他 MCP 宿主（含 Codex）：** 把 `previewUrl` 原样交给用户打开。出现登录页就先登录，再回到同一条地址。Codex 插件可能另有状态 Widget，那不是模拟器。
3. 再调 `get_xtapp_preview_status`。仍是 `need_login_or_open_page` 时，停下来，用同一条 URL 再打开一次。
4. 不要用浏览器去点模拟器 DOM。按键走 `send_xtapp_preview_input`，点选走 `send_xtapp_preview_touch`。设备截图走 `capture_xtapp_preview`。浏览器截图只能确认预览页已打开，不能代替模拟器截图。
5. MCP 重启后 session 复用本机 `~/.xtapp/codex-preview-session`，同一 URL 仍然有效。文件监听不会跨进程存活，每次预览都要再走一遍就绪检查。

`not_connected` / `need_login_or_open_page` 表示预览页没开、没登录，或打开的 URL 不是插件返回的那条。不要报成功。

人读状态：`need_login_or_open_page`、`running`、`timeout`、`page_open`。

## 素材

- 快照里每个素材都带 `key/path/mime/bytes/sha256/base64`。解析不出 key 的条目会出现在 `dropped`，不会被静默丢掉。
- 超过单次请求条数时，插件继续补发剩余素材；`assetKeys` 是工程完整清单。不要把 80 当成设备或工程上限。
- `.xic` 原样入库。`.png/.jpg/.webp` 由 Studio 转成 XIC，透明跟着源图的透明通道；白底图的白色会照样画出来。Proxy 不转码。
- 工具返回文本里如果出现 `未接受：…`，必须告诉用户哪些文件没进去，不要假装同步成功。

## 能力

- `run_xtapp_preview`：检查连接 → 同步当前 worktree → 启动或刷新。页没开时只返回 URL。若状态是 `stopped` 或 `error`，改走 `restart`。同一 worktree 复用已有文件监听，不会把刚同步完的 revision 立刻再推一遍。
- `restart_xtapp_preview`：先同步当前 worktree，再强制重新拉起 Lua Worker。必须带 `projectDir`。
- `sync_xtapp_preview_source`：只同步源码和素材，不启动。注意返回里的 `dropped`。
- `input`：模拟 `up/down/left/right/ok/back`。
- `send_xtapp_preview_touch`：默认点击方式，用逻辑坐标点画面。不要为了点选去改 Lua 增加测试槽。
- `tap_xtapp_preview_target`：若当前帧公布了带矩形的目标，插件会取其圆心再走坐标点击；没有目标时会明确说明，改用坐标或截图。
- 嵌套的 `domain/`、`persistence/`、`scripts/` Lua，以及 `data/`、`lang/` 下的 tsv/txt/json 会同步。看起来像源码但路径不合法的文件会出现在 `warnings`，不会被静默丢掉。
- 同一工程的源码推送串行执行；内容没变会跳过 HTTP。有上次成功 revision 时只 PATCH 变化，冲突则回退全量 POST。
- `stop`：停止当前 Worker。
- `capture_xtapp_preview`：截当前模拟器 PNG；优先用命令结果里的 `screenshot.dataUrl`。
- `/preview/context`：回传受限 Manifest、Lua 片段和最近日志。

右侧 widget 只报连接、应用名和 previewUrl，不是模拟器。Cursor 内置浏览器里打开的是同一张官网预览页。

## 诊断

按键不生效时，先查 `topic=input`，再调用 `inspect_xtapp_preview_context`。不要把 `queued` / `queued_timeout` / `not_connected` / `need_login_or_open_page` / `error` 报成运行成功。装完插件或重载 MCP 后需要新开一轮对话才会加载工具。
